docs.text: nf-binder-design Nextflow pipelines for de novo protein binder design. Overview This project provides Nextflow workflows for de novo design of protein binders: RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → AlphaFold2(initial guess) pipeline RFdiffusion Partial Diffusion for diversification and optimization RFdiffusion3 - RosettaCommons/foundry binder workflow: rfd3 (RFdiffusion3) → mpnn → rf3 (RosettaFold3) RFD4-Proteina - RosettaCommons/RFD4-Proteina sequence-structure co-design: rfd4_proteina BindCraft - parallel execution across multiple GPUs BindCraft2 - parallel execution across multiple GPUs, with modalities and composable design properties Germinal - antibody/nanobody design in parallel across multiple GPUs BoltzGen - design proteins and complexes using BoltzGen Fold Pulldown - an AlphaPulldown-like target × binder pulldown across multiple folding engines (AF2, Boltz-2, RF3, Protenix, AlphaFold3, OpenFold3, Chai-1, ESMFold2) Fold - multi-method structure prediction (AF2, Boltz-2, RF3, Protenix, AlphaFold3, OpenFold3, Chai-1, ESMFold2) with shared MSAs and EnGens clustering Every design workflow above can also run refold scoring ( --refold_with ): an independent validation step that folds selected designs again with one or more external predictors in addition to the workflow's initial evaluation. Features Flexible workflow options for different binder design strategies HPC-ready with support for SLURM and other job schedulers Multi-GPU parallelization for BindCraft trajectories Plugin system for custom design filters Comprehensive reporting with HTML outputs and summary statistics Quick Links Setup Instructions RFdiffusion Workflows RFdiffusion3 Workflow RFD4-Proteina Workflow BindCraft Workflow BindCraft2 Workflow Germinal Workflow BoltzGen Workflow Fold Pulldown Fold Refold Scoring FoldSeek Testing Development M3 HPC Examples Utility Scripts Examples GitHub Repository Release history License The pipeline code the comprises nf-binder-design is licensed under the MIT License. Note that some dependencies, packaged externally as containers, are under less permissive licenses: ⚠️ "Commercial Use Restrictions" Components of these workflows use RFdiffusion and BindCraft, which depend on PyRosetta/Rosetta. These are free for non-commercial use only . Commercial use requires a paid license agreement with University of Washington. See: Rosetta License Rosetta Licensing FAQ ⚠️ "Hosted Service Restriction" BindCraft2 ( --method bc2 ) is under a source-available, hosting-restricted license . It is free for any use, including commercial use, on your own or your organisation's infrastructure, and the designs it produces can be shared freely. It may not be provided to third parties as a hosted service (eg a web application, API, SaaS, or a tool or workflow step on a hosted platform) without a separate commercial license from the BindCraft2 copyright holders. Running the pipeline yourself, including Nextflow automatically pulling the BindCraft2 container, is permitted. See the BindCraft2 workflow docs for details. docs.text: Changelog All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. The format is based on Keep a Changelog , and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning . [Unreleased] Added --method bc2 (alias bindcraft2 ): parallel BindCraft2 binder design. Takes either a campaign settings JSON ( --bc2_config , with referenced target structures and scaffolds staged automatically) or flat params shared with --method bindcraft . Runs a fixed trajectory budget ( --bc2_n_traj , --bc2_batch_size ) with a distinct campaign_seed per batch, then gathers the batches with bindcraft campaign_output into one ranked summary plus an HTML report. Binder modalities via --bc2_modality (VHH, scFv, Fab, cyclic peptide, ...), composable design properties via --bc2_humanize , --bc2_protease_stable and friends, and every other BindCraft2 setting via --bc2_set 'KEY=VALUE;KEY=VALUE' . --hotspot_subsample draws a different subset of each target's hotspots per batch, in both input modes, seeded so the run still reproduces. --do_foldseek runs a FoldSeek structural novelty search over the ranked designs, searching only the binder chains. --complex_structures for --method fold_pulldown : supply target-binder complexes instead of a binder FASTA. The binder chain of each is folded against every target as usual, and the complex is then the reference its predictions are compared against, giving target_aligned_binder_rmsd_all , TM-score, DockQ and interface quality in complex_rmsd.tsv - one comparison per (target, engine, sample), all against the one complex that binder came from. This answers whether a binder still sits the same way against a different, longer or variant target. --binder_chains names the binder chain(s); several means several binder records per complex, named <complex>_<chain> . --target_chains chooses the superposition reference, defaulting to whichever chain is not a binder chain, so a two-chain complex needs only --binder_chains ; auto resolves it per complex by matching against the --targets records, for mixed-source complexes with inconsistent chain naming, and logs the chain it chose. --targets is optional here: without it the targets are read back out of the complexes' own target chains and deduplicated by sequence, and a set holding more than one distinct target stops the run rather than folding every binder against every target. A multi-chain target is not supported, since a pulldown folds two-chain pairs and there would be nothing to superimpose a second target chain onto. complex_rmsd.tsv carries a target column, which is what tells one binder's rows apart when it was folded against several. Refold scoring reports DockQ. combined_scores.tsv and refold_sample_scores.tsv gain <tool>_target_aligned_binder_dockq , with its _dockq_fnat , _dockq_fnonnat , _dockq_irmsd , _dockq_lrmsd , _interface_lddt and _clash_count companions, measuring the refolded complex against the design pose. On by default ( --refold_dockq false to drop them): the comparison reads structures that have already been written and needs no GPU, so it adds very little to a refold that has just paid for the folding. Only the target-aligned comparison gets them, since DockQ needs a receptor and a ligand and the whole-complex comparison puts both chains on both sides. Needs nf-binder-design-utils:0.1.8 . bin/rmsd4all.py --dockq : DockQ, its fnat / fnonnat / iRMSD / LRMSD components, interface lDDT and a clash count for a reference-versus-pose comparison, computed with peppr . The superimposition chains are the receptor and the scored chains the ligand, so a target-aligned binder comparison already names both. Agrees with the reference DockQ implementation to three decimal places on fnat , iRMSD and LRMSD ; unlike it, the receptor/ligand roles follow the chains given rather than chain size, which only changes LRMSD (and so DockQ) when the ligand is the larger chain. Residues are paired by sequence alignment and each pair keeps the atoms both structures carry, so a backbone-only design scores against an all-atom prediction on the backbone. Not yet exposed as a workflow parameter, and the nf-binder-design-utils container needs peppr before the Nextflow modules can pass --dockq . --method rfd4_proteina : binder design with RFD4-Proteina . The model co-designs sequence and structure, so there is no inverse-folding step between generation and scoring. An RFD4-Proteina condition spec ( --rfd4_config , YAML or JSON) is the default interface and gives access to the full conditioning vocabulary; --input_pdb with --contigs and --hotspot_res generates one using the upstream default recipe for protein binders. Designs are split across tasks by --rfd4_designs_per_task , each with its own seed. Supports structural filters ( --rfd4_filters ), Boltz-2 refold scoring ( --refold_with boltz ), FoldSeek search ( --do_foldseek ), partial diffusion and inverse folding. Runs in the rfd4-proteina:0.0.3-aaccdd2_of3_nv-cuda13 container, which is published for both amd64 and arm64 ( ..._arm64 ). On an arm64 host, add -c conf/platforms/arm64.config so the other steps use arm64 images too. Inline RFD4-Proteina metrics run by default ( --rfd4_metrics_tags ppi_refolding,hotspot_conditioning , false to disable) and --rfd4_recycle_strategy defaults to medium/front_loaded ; both can be overridden. --refold_with takes a list of engines: refold scoring is one path now, whichever predictor does the folding. Each design's binder sequence is folded against its target with every engine named - af2 , af2_mono , boltz , rf3 , protenix , af3 , openfold3 , chai1 , esmfold2 , esmfold2_fast - and every engine gives the same columns in combined_scores.tsv , prefixed with its name: confidence ( <tool>_iptm_max , <tool>_ipsae_max , <tool>_plddt_max , ...), RMSD against the design ( <tool>_target_aligned_binder_rmsd_all , <tool>_complex_rmsd_all ), the binder folded on its own ( <tool>_monomer_vs_design_rmsd_all , <tool>_monomer_vs_complex_rmsd_all ) and BindCraft interface metrics ( <tool>_interface_dG , ...). A cross-engine consensus_z ranks designs when more than one engine is named. New parameters: --refold_metrics , --refold_structure_stat , --refold_binder_monomer , --refold_monomer_single_sequence , --refold_interface_scoring . The new REFOLD subworkflow takes designs as tuple(meta, structure, scores) and holds nothing design-method-specific, so every design workflow uses it: rfd , rfd_partial , rfd3 , rfd4_proteina , bindcraft and germinal . --refold_target_fasta : refold the selected designs against a target other than the one they were built against, given as a FASTA of exactly one record. Without it the refold target is the target chain read back out of the design structures, so a binder designed against a truncated construct is only ever checked against that same truncated construct; this is how it is checked against the full-length protein instead, which is a different and harder question than the one the design run answered. One record only, because every binder is folded against every target and one row per design in refold_scores.tsv depends on there being a single target. The designs' own target is still read, and the run warns when the supplied sequence does not contain it - the usual sign that --refold_target_chain or the FASTA is not what the run assumed. Pair it with --templates for that target's structure and --target_msa or --create_target_msa for its MSA. With a longer target the refolded complex and the design are no longer the same molecule, so <tool>_complex_rmsd_all and <tool>_complex_tm_score_all come back as nan ; the structurally aligned _pruned variants and the target-aligned binder RMSD, which is the pose metric, are unaffected. --target_msa for --method fold_pulldown and for refolding: an A3M for the target built elsewhere, used instead of searching for one. Its first record must be the target sequence being folded. One file describes one target, so a pulldown over several stops rather than handing them all the same alignment, and it cannot be combined with --create_target_msa . This is the replacement for the old --full_refold_alignment / --refold_alignment . --method fold : multi-method structure folding for monomer and multimer/complex FASTA inputs with AF2, af2_mono (AF2 monomer weights on a chain-broken complex), Boltz-2, RosettaFold3, Protenix, AlphaFold3, OpenFold3, Chai-1, ESMFold2 and ESMFold2-Fast ( esmfold2_fast ). Shared MSAs (jackhmmer/HHblits or ColabFold, taxonomy-paired per engine for multimers), optional MSA subsampling, a per-structure score table (ipTM, pLDDT, ipSAE, pDockQ, LIS, ...) and EnGens clustering. AlphaFold3 weights are not bundled: download them under DeepMind's terms with models/download_af3_weights.sh , or point --af3_model_dir at them. ESMFold2 weights ship in its containers; esmfold2_fast always folds from sequence alone, and --esmfold2_single_sequence runs the full model MSA-free too. Also engens.nf for clustering an existing .cif / .pdb folder or glob. --method fold_pulldown : target × binder pulldown across the same engines, with per-structure scores, an aggregate summary (within-tool z-scores and a cross-engine consensus_z ) and a Quarto report. MSA cost is O(targets + binders) rather than O(targets × binders), and input ids are validated up front. Defaults to 5 structures per complex per engine ( --n_predictions ), with AF2 keeping all five models from its single run ( --af2_keep_models all ). --templates for --method fold / fold_pulldown : known structures ( .pdb / .cif , single chains or whole complexes) are matched to the chains being folded by sequence alignment, with no mapping file, and passed as per-chain templates to every engine except ESMFold2. Match cutoffs are --template_min_identity , --template_min_coverage , --template_min_aligned and --template_max_per_chain . fold_pulldown templates the target only unless --binder_templates , and by default holds Boltz's templated chains near their template ( --boltz_template_force , 1.0 Å). --boltz_refold_batch_size : fold several designs per Boltz refold task to amortise Boltz's per-invocation startup cost (default 1). AlphaFold3 can be run the way Germinal runs it, so an AF3 refold of Germinal designs is comparable to the scores that run produced. --af3_paired_msa false emits "pairedMsa": "" for every chain (no cross-chain pairing); --af3_templates search omits the templates key so AF3's own data pipeline searches pdb_seqres / mmcif_files for templates on every chain , which --af3_run_data_pipeline true and --af3_db_dir (the ~630 GB AF3 database set) enable. --af3_seeds also takes a comma list, putting every seed in one job's modelSeeds ; the seed list is then the replication, so the --n_predictions fan-out is suppressed and a run produces n_seeds × --af3_batch_size structures per complex. -profile af3_germinal_parity packages the whole combination with Germinal's target-only MSA mode and 5×5 sampling. Defaults are unchanged — without these AF3 still runs inference-only with a paired MSA and no templates. conf/platforms/arm64.config : run on arm64 / aarch64 workstations (eg NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10) by pointing the amd64-only images at their arm64 builds - nf-binder-design-utils:0.1.8-arm64 , boltz:v2.2.1-2_nv-cuda13-arm64 , foldseek:10-941cd33-arm64 , esmfold2:3.4.1.post1_nv-cuda13-arm64_{fast,full}_weights , rc-foundry:0.2.0_arm64-weights (RF3), bindcraft:nv-cuda13-arm64 and protenix:2026-09-21_85767b8_nv-cuda13-arm64_weights . Covers the RFD4-Proteina design path and its scoring, with boltz , esmfold2 , esmfold2_fast , rf3 and protenix available as refold engines; AF2, AF3, OpenFold3 and Chai-1 have no arm64 image yet. Two of those images need a GB10-specific build rather than only an architecture swap. RF3 uses the -ngc2606 tag rather than the plain 0.2.0_arm64-weights one: the latter is built on CUDA 12.8, whose nvrtc cannot target sm_121 , so on a GB10 it fails with nvrtc: error: invalid value for --gpu-architecture (-arch) when PyTorch's jiterator compiles erfinv . Protenix compiles its fused layer-norm extension at image build time for sm_70 to sm_100 only, so inference died at the first layer-norm call with no kernel image is available for execution on the device ; the arm64 image adds sm_120 and sm_121 and rebuilds it. Protenix also needs HOME set to a writable path when run as the host uid under Docker, which the config does, since it caches under $HOME/.cache and an unset HOME resolves to / . Use it alongside a runtime config, eg -c conf/platforms/arm64.config -c nextflow.docker.config . It also sets --gpu_devices all and --gpu_slots_per_device 1 : without --gpu_devices the GPU lock never engages and fold tasks run concurrently on the one device, which on a GB10 - where the 128 GB is shared between host and GPU - is enough to run it out of memory. refold/refold_sample_scores.tsv : one row per refolded sample, keyed by id , tool , batch and model , carrying that sample's own confidence, RMSD and interface scores with nothing reduced. combined_scores.tsv is one row per design, so every number in it is already a statistic over the samples; this table keeps the values those statistics were computed from, so min, max, mean, median or standard deviation over the samples can be worked out afterwards. --refold_structure_stat (default selected ): how several samples per design reduce to one value in the RMSD and interface columns of combined_scores.tsv . They now come from a single sample, the one the confidence ranking picks as best (by --consensus_metric , ipSAE), rather than a statistic per metric. The structural metrics all describe one set of coordinates, so taking the lowest RMSD and the lowest interface_dG independently gives a row that no predicted structure matches; and the interface metrics have no shared direction to take a best in anyway - interface_dG is better lower, interface_dSASA and interface_sc better higher. <tool>_selected_batch and <tool>_selected_model record which sample each design's structural columns came from - both, because an engine handed a list of seeds returns every sample from one batch. min|mean|max|first still apply one statistic to every structural column. --fold_seed_list (default true ): run --n_predictions as one invocation carrying every seed, for the engines that take a seed list and keep each seed's outputs apart. The alternative, one process per seed, loads the model that many times, and on a small complex the load is most of the wall time - ESMFold2-Fast measured 1m 8s per task on a GB10 for a two-chain complex, nearly all of it startup. Applies to esmfold2 , esmfold2_fast ( bin/fold/run_esmfold2.py now loops fold() over --seed with the model resident), openfold3 (its runner YAML's experiment_settings.seeds is already a list) and protenix ( runner/inference.py loops for seed in seeds: ). AF3 has the same ability under its own parameter, where a comma list in --af3_seeds already means "these seeds, one job". Boltz and RF3 are excluded because they are single-seed per process: Boltz calls seed_everything(seed) once, and RF3's inference engine config has seed: as a scalar. Set --fold_seed_list false to go back to one process per seed. GPU provenance trace. Every GPU task now records the device it ran on to <outdir>/logs/gpu_trace_<datestamp>.txt : timestamp, task hash, process, hostname, n_gpus , and the GPU index, UUID, model, driver version and total memory. New parameters: --gpu_trace_dir , --gpu_trace_file . Changed conf/platforms/monash_containers.config points every nf-binder-design-utils process at 0.1.8 on the Monash mirror. They were pinned at 0.1.6 and 0.1.5 , which predate the peppr dependency the refold's DockQ scoring needs, so a refold on M3 failed at the comparison step. The column order of refold_sample_scores.tsv and refold_scores.tsv is stable between runs. The RMSD tables were collected in arrival order, so which of the monomer and complex comparison blocks came first depended on which task finished first, and two runs over the same data could publish the same columns in a different order. --rf3_alignment is renamed to --rf3_target_msa , and a run that sets the old name stops with the new one named. Every MSA parameter in the pipeline now says "msa" - --target_msa , --create_target_msa , --create_binder_msa , --use_msa_server , --msa_method , --msa_subsample , --protenix_use_msa , --af3_paired_msa , --rf3_create_target_msa - with no *_alignment spelling left for an external MSA file. The design-time RF3 MSA keeps its --rf3_ engine prefix, which is what distinguishes it from the refold's --target_msa . Refold scoring is available in every design workflow, not just --method rfd4_proteina . --method rfd , rfd_partial , rfd3 , bindcraft and germinal all take --refold_with and run the same REFOLD subworkflow, giving the same engine-prefixed columns in their own combined_scores.tsv . Refolding is a held-out second opinion rather than a replacement for each workflow's own cofold: rfd and rfd_partial still run AF2 initial guess, rfd3 still runs RF3, and BindCraft and Germinal still run their own AF2 passes. That first cofold's scores are what the refold selects on, and refolding happens afterwards, on the designs worth the GPU time. The Boltz-only paths it replaces are gone: BOLTZ_REFOLD_CORE , BOLTZ_REFOLD_SCORING , BOLTZ_REFOLD_SCORING_RFD3 , BOLTZ_COMPARE_COMPLEX and BOLTZ_COMPARE_BINDER_MONOMER . In --method rfd and rfd_partial the AF2 initial guess scoring that always ran ( BINDCRAFT_SCORING plus COMBINE_SCORES ) is unchanged and still produces combined_scores.tsv when no refold engine is named; it is now the AF2IG_SCORING subworkflow. Which designs are refolded is chosen explicitly, by three parameters that compose, and every design that reached the step is accounted for in <refold_publish_dir>/refold_selection.tsv with its verdict, rank and sort value. --refold_filter is a threshold gate on the first cofold's scores, in the same semicolon-separated syntax as --rfd_filters ( --refold_filter 'ipsae>=0.5;pae_interaction<=10' ); it is decided per design, so refolding starts while the rest of the set is still being scored. --refold_sort_by ranks by one metric, with a - prefix for descending; on its own it selects nothing, since without a cap every design that passes the gate is refolded anyway. --refold_max caps how many go through: the best N with --refold_sort_by , the first N to be scored without it. A cap does not stream, with or without a ranking - the best N needs the last design scored, and the first N needs a count kept across every design. Write the descending form with an = ( --refold_sort_by='-ipsae' ), or Nextflow reads the leading - as one of its own options. A filter naming a metric the score table does not have stops the run and lists the columns that are there, rather than silently rejecting every design. Behaviour change for --method rfd3 : --refold_max no longer implies a ranking. --full_refold_filter_sort defaulted to pair_pae_min , so a capped refold took the best designs by that metric; its replacement --refold_sort_by defaults to unset, so a cap alone now takes the first N to finish, in whatever order that is. The run warns when --refold_max is set without --refold_sort_by . Add --refold_sort_by='pair_pae_min' to keep the old selection. Every refold parameter is spelled --refold_* . The --full_refold_* family is renamed without exception: --full_refold_with → --refold_with , --full_refold_max → --refold_max , --full_refold_rf3_batch_size → --refold_rf3_batch_size , and so on. --full_refold_filter_sort becomes --refold_sort_by . In --method rfd and rfd_partial , --refold_af2ig_filters becomes --refold_filter , which does the same thing in every workflow; the old name still works and warns. The refold's shared defaults move out of the workflow scripts into conf/refold.config (the --refold_* knobs, included for every entrypoint) and conf/refold_fold_stack.config (the fold stack a refold drives: --n_predictions , --msa_method , the --af2_* , --protenix_* and per-engine --refold_<engine>_* families, EnGens and FoldSeek). The second is included for the design workflows only: --method fold and --method fold_pulldown declare several of the same names with different values, and a config declaration beats a workflow script's default. Each workflow still declares its own --refold_publish_dir and --fold_publish_dir , which name a different directory in each. --method rfd3 's combined_scores.tsv carries the refold's engine-prefixed columns in place of the four Boltz-specific tables ( boltz_complex_* , boltz_monomer_* , boltz_target_aligned_binder_* , boltz_monomer_vs_complex_* ). --method rfd and rfd_partial likewise merge one refold table rather than three Boltz ones. rfd3 now writes binders.fasta with --refold_fasta_score_columns in the headers, as --method rfd4_proteina does. --boltz_refold_batch_size is removed. It batched several designs into one Boltz refold comparison task, and that Boltz-specific path no longer exists; the refold folds through the shared fold stack, where --refold_boltz_batch_size is samples per job. --refold_binder_chain / --refold_target_chain name the binder and target chains for the refold where the workflow has no derivation of its own, which is --method bindcraft and --method germinal (default binder B , target A ). rfd3 and rfd4_proteina still derive them from the contigs, and rfd / rfd_partial know them from how AF2 initial guess writes its complexes. Refold scoring is no longer Boltz-specific. BOLTZ_COMPARE_COMPLEX folded the complex and measured it against the design inside one process, which tied the metrics to one engine; folding, comparison and interface scoring are now separate steps that work from structures, so any engine's predictions go through the same scoring. --refold_oracles , which existed because the Boltz path could not take another engine, is deprecated and folded into --refold_with . Removed with it: --refold_create_target_msa , --refold_use_msa_server , --refold_alignment and --refold_target_templates - the refold takes its MSA and template choices from the fold stack ( --create_target_msa , --target_msa , --use_msa_server , --msa_method , --templates ), and a run that sets one of the old names stops with the replacement named. --refold_target_fasta keeps its name and its meaning (see Added). Column names change for --method rfd4_proteina : boltz_complex_plddt becomes boltz_plddt_max , while the RMSD columns keep their names. boltz_complex_pair_pae_min has no replacement: the engine-independent metric in its place is <tool>_pae_mean , the mean of the full PAE matrix. The refolded structures move from <outdir>/boltz_refold/ to <outdir>/rfd4_proteina/refold/ . The refold in --method rfd4_proteina now runs 5 structures per design per engine rather than 1, as 5 fold jobs of one sample each with seeds 42, 43, ... rather than one job of 5 samples. The engines that batch samples share a single trunk and recycling pass across them, so five samples from one seed differ only in the diffusion noise while five seeds re-run the whole prediction; the disadvantage is five model loads rather than one, roughly 45 s of fixed cost each for Boltz on a GB10. The split comes from per-engine batch sizes of 1, declared as --refold_<engine>_batch_size for the engines whose plain name nextflow.config already declares ( boltz , esmfold2 , chai1 , openfold3 , af3 , and rf3 as before) and as --protenix_batch_size for Protenix, which this workflow declares itself. Setting one higher gives that engine a mixture: --n_predictions 6 --refold_boltz_batch_size 3 is 2 seeds x 3 samples. --method fold and --method fold_pulldown are unchanged. The refold's long tables and the interface-score PDB names gain the fold batch ( <design>__<tool>__b<batch>.pdb ), because every job writes its single sample under the same model index and the batch is what tells two seeds' samples apart. RF3's engine flags are --refold_rf3_* in --method rfd4_proteina ( ckpt_path , num_steps , n_recycles , batch_size , early_stopping_plddt_threshold , seed ). The plain --rf3_* names belong to the design-time RF3 step in --method rfd3 , where --rf3_batch_size means MPNN designs per RF3 task rather than samples per fold job, and a workflow's parameters are one flat namespace. Where a workflow declares the prefixed names the fold stack reads only those ( modules/local/fold/common/fold_params.nf ), so a design-time value cannot leak into the refold. --method fold and --method fold_pulldown , which have no design-time RF3 step, keep the plain names. --protenix_seeds takes a comma list again. It was a hard error because Protenix separates its seeds by directory ( <name>/seed_<N>/predictions/ ) and not in the file name, so several seeds in one job collided in the flat fold/predictions/ gather and mis-paired their confidence files. PROTENIX_FOLD now reads the seed back out of the path and puts it into the names it publishes and scores ( foldNamingProtenixSeedBit ), which is what makes a seed list usable. Every structure predictor in --method fold / fold_pulldown ( af2 , af3 , boltz , esmfold2 , openfold3 , protenix , rf3 ) now honours task.ext.args , so extra engine CLI arguments can be set from config without a pipeline parameter for each option. ALPHAFOLD2 was the only one that did not. bin/foldseek/extract_design_chain.py takes --last-chains N to keep the last N chains instead of guessing the binder as the chain with fewest atoms, which picks the wrong chain for a multi-chain binder or a target smaller than its binder. ColabFold MSAs are published as {sequence_id}.a3m (e.g. PDL1.a3m ) rather than {fasta_stem}.N.a3m under a result/ folder. The pipeline parses under Nextflow's strict syntax (the v2 parser), so it runs on current Nextflow without NXF_SYNTAX_PARSER=v1 , while still supporting 24.04.3. The lib/ Groovy classes become Nextflow functions in modules/local/fold/common/ , named foldParamsEngine , foldNamingSampleLabel and so on in place of FoldParams.engine and FoldNaming.sampleLabel . main.nf includes every method's workflow rather than only the selected one, which adds a few seconds to startup since all ten are parsed on every run; --method still picks the one that runs, and each workflow's own parameter defaults stay private to it. In the platform configs, top-level def variables and helper functions become params or inline closures. Every method runs on 24.04.3, 24.10.0, 25.04.7 and 26.04.4, and the examples/*/run-m3*.sh scripts no longer export NXF_SYNTAX_PARSER=v1 . Lint with NXF_VER=25.04.7 nextflow lint -o concise main.nf workflows subworkflows modules nextflow.config conf tests . Removed --method boltz_pulldown , superseded by --method fold_pulldown : the same target × binder fan-out, MSA options and reporting, plus the other engines, per-chain template matching, multiple samples per pair and a cross-engine summary. --method fold_pulldown --methods boltz is the equivalent run, with structures written as mmCIF rather than PDB, --templates matched per chain rather than handed to Boltz wholesale, and the score table at fold_pulldown/fold_pulldown_scores.tsv . bin/find_available_gpu.py and the --gpu_allocation_detect_process_regex / --germinal_gpu_allocation_detect_process_regex parameters. The script's GPU-busy detection never worked inside Apptainer containers - Set --gpu_devices to enable the lock-based allocator instead. Fixed Boltz-2 fold and fold_pulldown of a homodimer failed with All proteins with the same sequence must share the same MSA! . Identical chains now share one MSA: the first chain's file, or one server MSA when that is what any copy would have used. BindCraft2 on the Monash M3 configs ( m3 , m3_bdi ) disables JAX GPU command buffers, which crashed the task intermittently. rf3 fold specs declare chain_type: polypeptide(L) for every sequence component. Without it, atomworks infers the chain type from the alphabet, so a low-complexity binder whose letters are all valid nucleotide codes - poly-alanine from a degenerate ProteinMPNN pass is the realistic case - was folded as RNA, and every comparison metric for that design came back NaN . The stack is protein-only, so the declaration is unconditional. From Nextflow 26, a publishDir path: or pattern: written as a plain string could not see the process's own inputs, so every method died at startup with No such variable: step / meta / batch_id before any task ran. The 18 such directives across 15 modules are closures now, which defers them to the task. This was independent of the strict syntax, and 24.04.3 was never affected. SILENT_FROM_PDBS referred to ${PATH} unescaped in an interpolated script block, so --method rfd died with No such variable: PATH before any silent file was written. FOLDSEEK_REMOTE_SEARCH passed $d unescaped to jq , so Nextflow tried to interpolate it instead of leaving it as the jq variable the query needs. PREPARE_RF3_TEMPLATE and RENAME_RF3_TEMPLATE_CHAINS had their publishDir directives inside the output: block, where they are not directives at all, so their templates were never published. An unset --refold_with stopped the run with unknown --methods entry '' instead of skipping the refold. BoltzGen input staging no longer replaces an absolute entity path with a symlink to itself when that file is already the staged input. Every design workflow failed to compile under Nextflow 24.04.x and 24.10.0 with Variable log already defined in the process scope , although manifest.nextflowVersion declares !>=23.04.0, <26.10 . The refold work reintroduced the pattern commit 6020de1 removed: inside a workflow body, an assignment whose right-hand side touches a script binding ( params , log , Channel , or another workflow-scope variable) cannot be declared with def under the pre-25 parser. The def s are dropped from those assignments in workflows/{rfd,rfd_partial,rfd3,rfd4_proteina,bindcraft,germinal}.nf and subworkflows/local/refold.nf ; foldValidationValidate (then FoldValidation.validate ) is unpacked by index rather than by destructuring, which the old parser rejects for the same reason. Every method now compiles on 24.04.3, 24.10.0, 25.04.7 and 26.04.4. tests/pipeline/compilation.nf.test gains germinal , rfd4_proteina and a refold-enabled rfd case, since the two workflows the regression reached had no compilation test at all. boltz_pae_mean was always blank while every other engine filled <tool>_pae_mean . Boltz's confidence JSON carries no PAE of any kind, but it does write the full matrix as pae_*.npz , already read for ipSAE; bin/parse_boltz_confidence.py --pae-npz now takes the mean off it in the same step, so the column is filled from the same numbers ipSAE is computed from. BindCraft reporting failed to render against matplotlib 3.11. Axes.boxplot 's labels keyword became tick_labels in 3.9 and is gone in 3.11, and the report has to run against whatever matplotlib the BindCraft image carries; it now picks the keyword from the signature once and uses it for all thirteen boxplots. Two fold runs in one workflow wrote their per-engine score tables to the same path, so the second overwrote the first and the merge downstream saw rows for complexes it never folded. The fold stack now takes a publish label ( FOLD , FOLD_PREDICT and each engine subworkflow), which the refold uses to keep the complex folds and the binder-monomer folds apart. bin/rmsd4all.py compared multi-chain structures in file order rather than in the order the --superimpose-chains / --score-chains lists gave, and rmsd_all pairs atoms by position. Two complexes holding the same chains but written in the opposite order - an RFD4-Proteina design, which writes the binder first, against a refold that writes the target first - had the binder measured against the target: 21 Å where the structures agree to 1.3 Å. The chains are now taken in the order asked for, which is what makes the two lists a statement of correspondence. BindCraft interface scoring of a Boltz-refolded complex was given the design's binder chain id, but the refolded complex has its own chain ids (binder A, target B). Wherever the design's binder was not chain A - --method rfd4_proteina , where it is B - every interface metric, and the sequence column beside them, described the target rather than the binder. rfd4_proteina: --rfd4_target_chain / --rfd4_binder_chain resolved to the literal string "false" when left unset, because the params default to boolean false and false.toString() is a non-empty, therefore truthy, string. The A/B default and the derivation from --contigs never ran, so filter metrics were computed on a chain that does not exist - every rg blank and every design rejected - and the binder sequence was read from the wrong chain. rfd4_proteina: the boltz_monomer_vs_complex_rmsd_* columns in combined_scores.tsv were always empty. The merge stripped _model_0.pdb / _monomer from the RMSD table's structure1 , but the values there end in _complex.pdb , so the key never matched a design id. --boltz_num_workers (default: task.cpus , unchanged): Boltz's dataloader workers deadlock on some platforms, leaving the run at 0% GPU indefinitely rather than failing. conf/platforms/arm64.config sets it to 0. Previously --num_workers was hardcoded to task.cpus in three modules and could not be overridden, since a duplicate flag in ext.args does not win. rfd4_proteina: COMBINE_RFD4_SCORES failed with Not a valid path value type whenever the filters rejected every design, because the empty-channel fallback passed Channel.of(file(...)) to ifEmpty , which takes a value rather than a channel. RF3 wrote its caches to $HOME , which is / when the container runs as a uid with no passwd entry - what conf/platforms/arm64.config asks for under Docker so a task can write its own work directory. rf3 fold died with PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/.cache' before any folding. RF3_FOLD and ROSETTAFOLD3 now set XDG_CACHE_HOME , XDG_CONFIG_HOME and TRITON_CACHE_DIR inside the task directory, as the Boltz module already did. rfd3: treat unset/ false --rf3_batch_size as 1 (avoids Boolean→Integer cast failure when a shared config sentinel is present). The GPU lock ( --gpu_devices ) failed whenever the tasks sharing it did not all run as the same user. Some images run as root and others are pinned to the invoking user ( conf/platforms/arm64.config does this under Docker), and the lock files take the ownership of whichever task created them, so a task running as anyone else could not open one for writing and waited out --gpu_lock_timeout before failing. bin/gpu_lock.sh now creates the lock directory and its files world-writable, and a lock file it cannot write is reported once and fails the task immediately rather than being waited on. The GPU trace directory is created the same way; a trace row written by a task running as another user was previously dropped in silence. A lock directory left behind by an earlier run has to be deleted for the new permissions to take effect. examples/pdl1-rfd/run-m3-full.sh and examples/pdl1-bindcraft/run-m3.sh : point at repo main.nf , pin NXF_VER=24.10.0 , and drop mid-command # comments that broke the Nextflow invocation. Remove unused random_choice helper from conf/platforms/m3.config . Some parameter validation for bindcraft.nf . Write params.json to output directory. Changed Move 'filtering' result folder to 'rfdiffison/filtered' Don't output redundant .tsv files to the results directory. Changed default --pmpnn_relax_cycles from 0 to 3 Made default queue size 1, for single local GPU mode. Added m3-bdi.config , site specific for M3/MASSIVE HPC cluster. Use the nf-binder-design-utils container instead of mdanalysis . Update config and docs to use -profile for site-specifc configurations Fixed Fixed Quarto rendering permissions issues (copy Qmd to work folder). [0.1.4] - 2025-08-12 Added BindCraft end-to-end workflow with basic HTML report GPU allocation heuristics for local multi-GPU workstations. HyperMPNN weights download script ( models/download_hypermpnn_weights.sh ). New runnable examples in examples/ . Changed RFDiffusion --hotspot_res no longer requires brackets in main.nf . Minor tweaks to site-specific configs for m3 and mlerp . [0.1.3] - 2025-07-11 Added A plugin system for filtering designs based on calculated metrics. --rfd_filters parameter to apply filters to RFDiffusion backbones (e.g., --rfd_filters "rg<25" ). Initial filter plugin for radius of gyration ( rg ). Integration of BindCraft-derived scoring of designs, as extra_scores.tsv . This adds metrics including: Interface score, shape complementarity, dG, and dSASA. Secondary structure percentages (helix, sheet, loop) for the binder and interface. Unrelaxed and relaxed clash scores. Hotspot and target RMSD. Sequence-based metrics like extinction coefficient. --pmpnn_omit_aas flag to exclude certain amino acids from designs (default 'CX'). --rfd_compress_trajectories flag to gzip RFDiffusion traj/*.pdb files (default true ). Changed Filtering results are now saved to a subdirectory named after the pipeline step (in filtering/rfdiffusion/ ). The score merging script ( merge_scores.py ) was improved to be more robust and handle an arbitrary number of score files. Use more lightweight container for get_contigs.nf and renumber_residues.nf modules. Fixed The gpu_device parameter is now correctly passed to the partial diffusion process, allowing proper GPU selection. [0.1.2] - 2025-06-19 Added Added the boltz_pulldown.nf protocol. Allow gpu device to be selected. Support relaxation in ProteinMPNN ( pmpnn_relax_cycles can now be non-zero) Changed Change dl_binder_design output filenaming (include "_mpnn{n}" suffix) Change RFDiffusion config handling when unspecified Docs: Add APPTAINER_TMPDIR and NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR advice to M3-specific docs Fixed Fix get_contigs for multi-chain targets. Fix failure that occurred when using --rfd_batch_size > 1. [0.1.1] - 2025-04-04 Changed Update to use containers from Github package registry [0.1] - 2025-03-24 Added Initial version with RFDiffusion->ProteinMPNN->af2_initial_guess binder design and partial diffusion pipelines.

docs.text: --method bc2 (alias bindcraft2 ): parallel BindCraft2 binder design. Takes either a campaign settings JSON ( --bc2_config , with referenced target structures and scaffolds staged automatically) or flat params shared with --method bindcraft . Runs a fixed trajectory budget ( --bc2_n_traj , --bc2_batch_size ) with a distinct campaign_seed per batch, then gathers the batches with bindcraft campaign_output into one ranked summary plus an HTML report. Binder modalities via --bc2_modality (VHH, scFv, Fab, cyclic peptide, ...), composable design properties via --bc2_humanize , --bc2_protease_stable and friends, and every other BindCraft2 setting via --bc2_set 'KEY=VALUE;KEY=VALUE' . --hotspot_subsample draws a different subset of each target's hotspots per batch, in both input modes, seeded so the run still reproduces. --do_foldseek runs a FoldSeek structural novelty search over the ranked designs, searching only the binder chains. --complex_structures for --method fold_pulldown : supply target-binder complexes instead of a binder FASTA. The binder chain of each is folded against every target as usual, and the complex is then the reference its predictions are compared against, giving target_aligned_binder_rmsd_all , TM-score, DockQ and interface quality in complex_rmsd.tsv - one comparison per (target, engine, sample), all against the one complex that binder came from. This answers whether a binder still sits the same way against a different, longer or variant target. --binder_chains names the binder chain(s); several means several binder records per complex, named <complex>_<chain> . --target_chains chooses the superposition reference, defaulting to whichever chain is not a binder chain, so a two-chain complex needs only --binder_chains ; auto resolves it per complex by matching against the --targets records, for mixed-source complexes with inconsistent chain naming, and logs the chain it chose. --targets is optional here: without it the targets are read back out of the complexes' own target chains and deduplicated by sequence, and a set holding more than one distinct target stops the run rather than folding every binder against every target. A multi-chain target is not supported, since a pulldown folds two-chain pairs and there would be nothing to superimpose a second target chain onto. complex_rmsd.tsv carries a target column, which is what tells one binder's rows apart when it was folded against several. Refold scoring reports DockQ. combined_scores.tsv and refold_sample_scores.tsv gain <tool>_target_aligned_binder_dockq , with its _dockq_fnat , _dockq_fnonnat , _dockq_irmsd , _dockq_lrmsd , _interface_lddt and _clash_count companions, measuring the refolded complex against the design pose. On by default ( --refold_dockq false to drop them): the comparison reads structures that have already been written and needs no GPU, so it adds very little to a refold that has just paid for the folding. Only the target-aligned comparison gets them, since DockQ needs a receptor and a ligand and the whole-complex comparison puts both chains on both sides. Needs nf-binder-design-utils:0.1.8 . bin/rmsd4all.py --dockq : DockQ, its fnat / fnonnat / iRMSD / LRMSD components, interface lDDT and a clash count for a reference-versus-pose comparison, computed with peppr . The superimposition chains are the receptor and the scored chains the ligand, so a target-aligned binder comparison already names both. Agrees with the reference DockQ implementation to three decimal places on fnat , iRMSD and LRMSD ; unlike it, the receptor/ligand roles follow the chains given rather than chain size, which only changes LRMSD (and so DockQ) when the ligand is the larger chain. Residues are paired by sequence alignment and each pair keeps the atoms both structures carry, so a backbone-only design scores against an all-atom prediction on the backbone. Not yet exposed as a workflow parameter, and the nf-binder-design-utils container needs peppr before the Nextflow modules can pass --dockq . --method rfd4_proteina : binder design with RFD4-Proteina . The model co-designs sequence and structure, so there is no inverse-folding step between generation and scoring. An RFD4-Proteina condition spec ( --rfd4_config , YAML or JSON) is the default interface and gives access to the full conditioning vocabulary; --input_pdb with --contigs and --hotspot_res generates one using the upstream default recipe for protein binders. Designs are split across tasks by --rfd4_designs_per_task , each with its own seed. Supports structural filters ( --rfd4_filters ), Boltz-2 refold scoring ( --refold_with boltz ), FoldSeek search ( --do_foldseek ), partial diffusion and inverse folding. Runs in the rfd4-proteina:0.0.3-aaccdd2_of3_nv-cuda13 container, which is published for both amd64 and arm64 ( ..._arm64 ). On an arm64 host, add -c conf/platforms/arm64.config so the other steps use arm64 images too. Inline RFD4-Proteina metrics run by default ( --rfd4_metrics_tags ppi_refolding,hotspot_conditioning , false to disable) and --rfd4_recycle_strategy defaults to medium/front_loaded ; both can be overridden. --refold_with takes a list of engines: refold scoring is one path now, whichever predictor does the folding. Each design's binder sequence is folded against its target with every engine named - af2 , af2_mono , boltz , rf3 , protenix , af3 , openfold3 , chai1 , esmfold2 , esmfold2_fast - and every engine gives the same columns in combined_scores.tsv , prefixed with its name: confidence ( <tool>_iptm_max , <tool>_ipsae_max , <tool>_plddt_max , ...), RMSD against the design ( <tool>_target_aligned_binder_rmsd_all , <tool>_complex_rmsd_all ), the binder folded on its own ( <tool>_monomer_vs_design_rmsd_all , <tool>_monomer_vs_complex_rmsd_all ) and BindCraft interface metrics ( <tool>_interface_dG , ...). A cross-engine consensus_z ranks designs when more than one engine is named. New parameters: --refold_metrics , --refold_structure_stat , --refold_binder_monomer , --refold_monomer_single_sequence , --refold_interface_scoring . The new REFOLD subworkflow takes designs as tuple(meta, structure, scores) and holds nothing design-method-specific, so every design workflow uses it: rfd , rfd_partial , rfd3 , rfd4_proteina , bindcraft and germinal . --refold_target_fasta : refold the selected designs against a target other than the one they were built against, given as a FASTA of exactly one record. Without it the refold target is the target chain read back out of the design structures, so a binder designed against a truncated construct is only ever checked against that same truncated construct; this is how it is checked against the full-length protein instead, which is a different and harder question than the one the design run answered. One record only, because every binder is folded against every target and one row per design in refold_scores.tsv depends on there being a single target. The designs' own target is still read, and the run warns when the supplied sequence does not contain it - the usual sign that --refold_target_chain or the FASTA is not what the run assumed. Pair it with --templates for that target's structure and --target_msa or --create_target_msa for its MSA. With a longer target the refolded complex and the design are no longer the same molecule, so <tool>_complex_rmsd_all and <tool>_complex_tm_score_all come back as nan ; the structurally aligned _pruned variants and the target-aligned binder RMSD, which is the pose metric, are unaffected. --target_msa for --method fold_pulldown and for refolding: an A3M for the target built elsewhere, used instead of searching for one. Its first record must be the target sequence being folded. One file describes one target, so a pulldown over several stops rather than handing them all the same alignment, and it cannot be combined with --create_target_msa . This is the replacement for the old --full_refold_alignment / --refold_alignment . --method fold : multi-method structure folding for monomer and multimer/complex FASTA inputs with AF2, af2_mono (AF2 monomer weights on a chain-broken complex), Boltz-2, RosettaFold3, Protenix, AlphaFold3, OpenFold3, Chai-1, ESMFold2 and ESMFold2-Fast ( esmfold2_fast ). Shared MSAs (jackhmmer/HHblits or ColabFold, taxonomy-paired per engine for multimers), optional MSA subsampling, a per-structure score table (ipTM, pLDDT, ipSAE, pDockQ, LIS, ...) and EnGens clustering. AlphaFold3 weights are not bundled: download them under DeepMind's terms with models/download_af3_weights.sh , or point --af3_model_dir at them. ESMFold2 weights ship in its containers; esmfold2_fast always folds from sequence alone, and --esmfold2_single_sequence runs the full model MSA-free too. Also engens.nf for clustering an existing .cif / .pdb folder or glob. --method fold_pulldown : target × binder pulldown across the same engines, with per-structure scores, an aggregate summary (within-tool z-scores and a cross-engine consensus_z ) and a Quarto report. MSA cost is O(targets + binders) rather than O(targets × binders), and input ids are validated up front. Defaults to 5 structures per complex per engine ( --n_predictions ), with AF2 keeping all five models from its single run ( --af2_keep_models all ). --templates for --method fold / fold_pulldown : known structures ( .pdb / .cif , single chains or whole complexes) are matched to the chains being folded by sequence alignment, with no mapping file, and passed as per-chain templates to every engine except ESMFold2. Match cutoffs are --template_min_identity , --template_min_coverage , --template_min_aligned and --template_max_per_chain . fold_pulldown templates the target only unless --binder_templates , and by default holds Boltz's templated chains near their template ( --boltz_template_force , 1.0 Å). --boltz_refold_batch_size : fold several designs per Boltz refold task to amortise Boltz's per-invocation startup cost (default 1). AlphaFold3 can be run the way Germinal runs it, so an AF3 refold of Germinal designs is comparable to the scores that run produced. --af3_paired_msa false emits "pairedMsa": "" for every chain (no cross-chain pairing); --af3_templates search omits the templates key so AF3's own data pipeline searches pdb_seqres / mmcif_files for templates on every chain , which --af3_run_data_pipeline true and --af3_db_dir (the ~630 GB AF3 database set) enable. --af3_seeds also takes a comma list, putting every seed in one job's modelSeeds ; the seed list is then the replication, so the --n_predictions fan-out is suppressed and a run produces n_seeds × --af3_batch_size structures per complex. -profile af3_germinal_parity packages the whole combination with Germinal's target-only MSA mode and 5×5 sampling. Defaults are unchanged — without these AF3 still runs inference-only with a paired MSA and no templates. conf/platforms/arm64.config : run on arm64 / aarch64 workstations (eg NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10) by pointing the amd64-only images at their arm64 builds - nf-binder-design-utils:0.1.8-arm64 , boltz:v2.2.1-2_nv-cuda13-arm64 , foldseek:10-941cd33-arm64 , esmfold2:3.4.1.post1_nv-cuda13-arm64_{fast,full}_weights , rc-foundry:0.2.0_arm64-weights (RF3), bindcraft:nv-cuda13-arm64 and protenix:2026-09-21_85767b8_nv-cuda13-arm64_weights . Covers the RFD4-Proteina design path and its scoring, with boltz , esmfold2 , esmfold2_fast , rf3 and protenix available as refold engines; AF2, AF3, OpenFold3 and Chai-1 have no arm64 image yet. Two of those images need a GB10-specific build rather than only an architecture swap. RF3 uses the -ngc2606 tag rather than the plain 0.2.0_arm64-weights one: the latter is built on CUDA 12.8, whose nvrtc cannot target sm_121 , so on a GB10 it fails with nvrtc: error: invalid value for --gpu-architecture (-arch) when PyTorch's jiterator compiles erfinv . Protenix compiles its fused layer-norm extension at image build time for sm_70 to sm_100 only, so inference died at the first layer-norm call with no kernel image is available for execution on the device ; the arm64 image adds sm_120 and sm_121 and rebuilds it. Protenix also needs HOME set to a writable path when run as the host uid under Docker, which the config does, since it caches under $HOME/.cache and an unset HOME resolves to / . Use it alongside a runtime config, eg -c conf/platforms/arm64.config -c nextflow.docker.config . It also sets --gpu_devices all and --gpu_slots_per_device 1 : without --gpu_devices the GPU lock never engages and fold tasks run concurrently on the one device, which on a GB10 - where the 128 GB is shared between host and GPU - is enough to run it out of memory. refold/refold_sample_scores.tsv : one row per refolded sample, keyed by id , tool , batch and model , carrying that sample's own confidence, RMSD and interface scores with nothing reduced. combined_scores.tsv is one row per design, so every number in it is already a statistic over the samples; this table keeps the values those statistics were computed from, so min, max, mean, median or standard deviation over the samples can be worked out afterwards. --refold_structure_stat (default selected ): how several samples per design reduce to one value in the RMSD and interface columns of combined_scores.tsv . They now come from a single sample, the one the confidence ranking picks as best (by --consensus_metric , ipSAE), rather than a statistic per metric. The structural metrics all describe one set of coordinates, so taking the lowest RMSD and the lowest interface_dG independently gives a row that no predicted structure matches; and the interface metrics have no shared direction to take a best in anyway - interface_dG is better lower, interface_dSASA and interface_sc better higher. <tool>_selected_batch and <tool>_selected_model record which sample each design's structural columns came from - both, because an engine handed a list of seeds returns every sample from one batch. min|mean|max|first still apply one statistic to every structural column. --fold_seed_list (default true ): run --n_predictions as one invocation carrying every seed, for the engines that take a seed list and keep each seed's outputs apart. The alternative, one process per seed, loads the model that many times, and on a small complex the load is most of the wall time - ESMFold2-Fast measured 1m 8s per task on a GB10 for a two-chain complex, nearly all of it startup. Applies to esmfold2 , esmfold2_fast ( bin/fold/run_esmfold2.py now loops fold() over --seed with the model resident), openfold3 (its runner YAML's experiment_settings.seeds is already a list) and protenix ( runner/inference.py loops for seed in seeds: ). AF3 has the same ability under its own parameter, where a comma list in --af3_seeds already means "these seeds, one job". Boltz and RF3 are excluded because they are single-seed per process: Boltz calls seed_everything(seed) once, and RF3's inference engine config has seed: as a scalar. Set --fold_seed_list false to go back to one process per seed. GPU provenance trace. Every GPU task now records the device it ran on to <outdir>/logs/gpu_trace_<datestamp>.txt : timestamp, task hash, process, hostname, n_gpus , and the GPU index, UUID, model, driver version and total memory. New parameters: --gpu_trace_dir , --gpu_trace_file .

docs.text: conf/platforms/monash_containers.config points every nf-binder-design-utils process at 0.1.8 on the Monash mirror. They were pinned at 0.1.6 and 0.1.5 , which predate the peppr dependency the refold's DockQ scoring needs, so a refold on M3 failed at the comparison step. The column order of refold_sample_scores.tsv and refold_scores.tsv is stable between runs. The RMSD tables were collected in arrival order, so which of the monomer and complex comparison blocks came first depended on which task finished first, and two runs over the same data could publish the same columns in a different order. --rf3_alignment is renamed to --rf3_target_msa , and a run that sets the old name stops with the new one named. Every MSA parameter in the pipeline now says "msa" - --target_msa , --create_target_msa , --create_binder_msa , --use_msa_server , --msa_method , --msa_subsample , --protenix_use_msa , --af3_paired_msa , --rf3_create_target_msa - with no *_alignment spelling left for an external MSA file. The design-time RF3 MSA keeps its --rf3_ engine prefix, which is what distinguishes it from the refold's --target_msa . Refold scoring is available in every design workflow, not just --method rfd4_proteina . --method rfd , rfd_partial , rfd3 , bindcraft and germinal all take --refold_with and run the same REFOLD subworkflow, giving the same engine-prefixed columns in their own combined_scores.tsv . Refolding is a held-out second opinion rather than a replacement for each workflow's own cofold: rfd and rfd_partial still run AF2 initial guess, rfd3 still runs RF3, and BindCraft and Germinal still run their own AF2 passes. That first cofold's scores are what the refold selects on, and refolding happens afterwards, on the designs worth the GPU time. The Boltz-only paths it replaces are gone: BOLTZ_REFOLD_CORE , BOLTZ_REFOLD_SCORING , BOLTZ_REFOLD_SCORING_RFD3 , BOLTZ_COMPARE_COMPLEX and BOLTZ_COMPARE_BINDER_MONOMER . In --method rfd and rfd_partial the AF2 initial guess scoring that always ran ( BINDCRAFT_SCORING plus COMBINE_SCORES ) is unchanged and still produces combined_scores.tsv when no refold engine is named; it is now the AF2IG_SCORING subworkflow. Which designs are refolded is chosen explicitly, by three parameters that compose, and every design that reached the step is accounted for in <refold_publish_dir>/refold_selection.tsv with its verdict, rank and sort value. --refold_filter is a threshold gate on the first cofold's scores, in the same semicolon-separated syntax as --rfd_filters ( --refold_filter 'ipsae>=0.5;pae_interaction<=10' ); it is decided per design, so refolding starts while the rest of the set is still being scored. --refold_sort_by ranks by one metric, with a - prefix for descending; on its own it selects nothing, since without a cap every design that passes the gate is refolded anyway. --refold_max caps how many go through: the best N with --refold_sort_by , the first N to be scored without it. A cap does not stream, with or without a ranking - the best N needs the last design scored, and the first N needs a count kept across every design. Write the descending form with an = ( --refold_sort_by='-ipsae' ), or Nextflow reads the leading - as one of its own options. A filter naming a metric the score table does not have stops the run and lists the columns that are there, rather than silently rejecting every design. Behaviour change for --method rfd3 : --refold_max no longer implies a ranking. --full_refold_filter_sort defaulted to pair_pae_min , so a capped refold took the best designs by that metric; its replacement --refold_sort_by defaults to unset, so a cap alone now takes the first N to finish, in whatever order that is. The run warns when --refold_max is set without --refold_sort_by . Add --refold_sort_by='pair_pae_min' to keep the old selection. Every refold parameter is spelled --refold_* . The --full_refold_* family is renamed without exception: --full_refold_with → --refold_with , --full_refold_max → --refold_max , --full_refold_rf3_batch_size → --refold_rf3_batch_size , and so on. --full_refold_filter_sort becomes --refold_sort_by . In --method rfd and rfd_partial , --refold_af2ig_filters becomes --refold_filter , which does the same thing in every workflow; the old name still works and warns. The refold's shared defaults move out of the workflow scripts into conf/refold.config (the --refold_* knobs, included for every entrypoint) and conf/refold_fold_stack.config (the fold stack a refold drives: --n_predictions , --msa_method , the --af2_* , --protenix_* and per-engine --refold_<engine>_* families, EnGens and FoldSeek). The second is included for the design workflows only: --method fold and --method fold_pulldown declare several of the same names with different values, and a config declaration beats a workflow script's default. Each workflow still declares its own --refold_publish_dir and --fold_publish_dir , which name a different directory in each. --method rfd3 's combined_scores.tsv carries the refold's engine-prefixed columns in place of the four Boltz-specific tables ( boltz_complex_* , boltz_monomer_* , boltz_target_aligned_binder_* , boltz_monomer_vs_complex_* ). --method rfd and rfd_partial likewise merge one refold table rather than three Boltz ones. rfd3 now writes binders.fasta with --refold_fasta_score_columns in the headers, as --method rfd4_proteina does. --boltz_refold_batch_size is removed. It batched several designs into one Boltz refold comparison task, and that Boltz-specific path no longer exists; the refold folds through the shared fold stack, where --refold_boltz_batch_size is samples per job. --refold_binder_chain / --refold_target_chain name the binder and target chains for the refold where the workflow has no derivation of its own, which is --method bindcraft and --method germinal (default binder B , target A ). rfd3 and rfd4_proteina still derive them from the contigs, and rfd / rfd_partial know them from how AF2 initial guess writes its complexes. Refold scoring is no longer Boltz-specific. BOLTZ_COMPARE_COMPLEX folded the complex and measured it against the design inside one process, which tied the metrics to one engine; folding, comparison and interface scoring are now separate steps that work from structures, so any engine's predictions go through the same scoring. --refold_oracles , which existed because the Boltz path could not take another engine, is deprecated and folded into --refold_with . Removed with it: --refold_create_target_msa , --refold_use_msa_server , --refold_alignment and --refold_target_templates - the refold takes its MSA and template choices from the fold stack ( --create_target_msa , --target_msa , --use_msa_server , --msa_method , --templates ), and a run that sets one of the old names stops with the replacement named. --refold_target_fasta keeps its name and its meaning (see Added). Column names change for --method rfd4_proteina : boltz_complex_plddt becomes boltz_plddt_max , while the RMSD columns keep their names. boltz_complex_pair_pae_min has no replacement: the engine-independent metric in its place is <tool>_pae_mean , the mean of the full PAE matrix. The refolded structures move from <outdir>/boltz_refold/ to <outdir>/rfd4_proteina/refold/ . The refold in --method rfd4_proteina now runs 5 structures per design per engine rather than 1, as 5 fold jobs of one sample each with seeds 42, 43, ... rather than one job of 5 samples. The engines that batch samples share a single trunk and recycling pass across them, so five samples from one seed differ only in the diffusion noise while five seeds re-run the whole prediction; the disadvantage is five model loads rather than one, roughly 45 s of fixed cost each for Boltz on a GB10. The split comes from per-engine batch sizes of 1, declared as --refold_<engine>_batch_size for the engines whose plain name nextflow.config already declares ( boltz , esmfold2 , chai1 , openfold3 , af3 , and rf3 as before) and as --protenix_batch_size for Protenix, which this workflow declares itself. Setting one higher gives that engine a mixture: --n_predictions 6 --refold_boltz_batch_size 3 is 2 seeds x 3 samples. --method fold and --method fold_pulldown are unchanged. The refold's long tables and the interface-score PDB names gain the fold batch ( <design>__<tool>__b<batch>.pdb ), because every job writes its single sample under the same model index and the batch is what tells two seeds' samples apart. RF3's engine flags are --refold_rf3_* in --method rfd4_proteina ( ckpt_path , num_steps , n_recycles , batch_size , early_stopping_plddt_threshold , seed ). The plain --rf3_* names belong to the design-time RF3 step in --method rfd3 , where --rf3_batch_size means MPNN designs per RF3 task rather than samples per fold job, and a workflow's parameters are one flat namespace. Where a workflow declares the prefixed names the fold stack reads only those ( modules/local/fold/common/fold_params.nf ), so a design-time value cannot leak into the refold. --method fold and --method fold_pulldown , which have no design-time RF3 step, keep the plain names. --protenix_seeds takes a comma list again. It was a hard error because Protenix separates its seeds by directory ( <name>/seed_<N>/predictions/ ) and not in the file name, so several seeds in one job collided in the flat fold/predictions/ gather and mis-paired their confidence files. PROTENIX_FOLD now reads the seed back out of the path and puts it into the names it publishes and scores ( foldNamingProtenixSeedBit ), which is what makes a seed list usable. Every structure predictor in --method fold / fold_pulldown ( af2 , af3 , boltz , esmfold2 , openfold3 , protenix , rf3 ) now honours task.ext.args , so extra engine CLI arguments can be set from config without a pipeline parameter for each option. ALPHAFOLD2 was the only one that did not. bin/foldseek/extract_design_chain.py takes --last-chains N to keep the last N chains instead of guessing the binder as the chain with fewest atoms, which picks the wrong chain for a multi-chain binder or a target smaller than its binder. ColabFold MSAs are published as {sequence_id}.a3m (e.g. PDL1.a3m ) rather than {fasta_stem}.N.a3m under a result/ folder. The pipeline parses under Nextflow's strict syntax (the v2 parser), so it runs on current Nextflow without NXF_SYNTAX_PARSER=v1 , while still supporting 24.04.3. The lib/ Groovy classes become Nextflow functions in modules/local/fold/common/ , named foldParamsEngine , foldNamingSampleLabel and so on in place of FoldParams.engine and FoldNaming.sampleLabel . main.nf includes every method's workflow rather than only the selected one, which adds a few seconds to startup since all ten are parsed on every run; --method still picks the one that runs, and each workflow's own parameter defaults stay private to it. In the platform configs, top-level def variables and helper functions become params or inline closures. Every method runs on 24.04.3, 24.10.0, 25.04.7 and 26.04.4, and the examples/*/run-m3*.sh scripts no longer export NXF_SYNTAX_PARSER=v1 . Lint with NXF_VER=25.04.7 nextflow lint -o concise main.nf workflows subworkflows modules nextflow.config conf tests .

docs.text: --method boltz_pulldown , superseded by --method fold_pulldown : the same target × binder fan-out, MSA options and reporting, plus the other engines, per-chain template matching, multiple samples per pair and a cross-engine summary. --method fold_pulldown --methods boltz is the equivalent run, with structures written as mmCIF rather than PDB, --templates matched per chain rather than handed to Boltz wholesale, and the score table at fold_pulldown/fold_pulldown_scores.tsv . bin/find_available_gpu.py and the --gpu_allocation_detect_process_regex / --germinal_gpu_allocation_detect_process_regex parameters. The script's GPU-busy detection never worked inside Apptainer containers - Set --gpu_devices to enable the lock-based allocator instead.

docs.text: Boltz-2 fold and fold_pulldown of a homodimer failed with All proteins with the same sequence must share the same MSA! . Identical chains now share one MSA: the first chain's file, or one server MSA when that is what any copy would have used. BindCraft2 on the Monash M3 configs ( m3 , m3_bdi ) disables JAX GPU command buffers, which crashed the task intermittently. rf3 fold specs declare chain_type: polypeptide(L) for every sequence component. Without it, atomworks infers the chain type from the alphabet, so a low-complexity binder whose letters are all valid nucleotide codes - poly-alanine from a degenerate ProteinMPNN pass is the realistic case - was folded as RNA, and every comparison metric for that design came back NaN . The stack is protein-only, so the declaration is unconditional. From Nextflow 26, a publishDir path: or pattern: written as a plain string could not see the process's own inputs, so every method died at startup with No such variable: step / meta / batch_id before any task ran. The 18 such directives across 15 modules are closures now, which defers them to the task. This was independent of the strict syntax, and 24.04.3 was never affected. SILENT_FROM_PDBS referred to ${PATH} unescaped in an interpolated script block, so --method rfd died with No such variable: PATH before any silent file was written. FOLDSEEK_REMOTE_SEARCH passed $d unescaped to jq , so Nextflow tried to interpolate it instead of leaving it as the jq variable the query needs. PREPARE_RF3_TEMPLATE and RENAME_RF3_TEMPLATE_CHAINS had their publishDir directives inside the output: block, where they are not directives at all, so their templates were never published. An unset --refold_with stopped the run with unknown --methods entry '' instead of skipping the refold. BoltzGen input staging no longer replaces an absolute entity path with a symlink to itself when that file is already the staged input. Every design workflow failed to compile under Nextflow 24.04.x and 24.10.0 with Variable log already defined in the process scope , although manifest.nextflowVersion declares !>=23.04.0, <26.10 . The refold work reintroduced the pattern commit 6020de1 removed: inside a workflow body, an assignment whose right-hand side touches a script binding ( params , log , Channel , or another workflow-scope variable) cannot be declared with def under the pre-25 parser. The def s are dropped from those assignments in workflows/{rfd,rfd_partial,rfd3,rfd4_proteina,bindcraft,germinal}.nf and subworkflows/local/refold.nf ; foldValidationValidate (then FoldValidation.validate ) is unpacked by index rather than by destructuring, which the old parser rejects for the same reason. Every method now compiles on 24.04.3, 24.10.0, 25.04.7 and 26.04.4. tests/pipeline/compilation.nf.test gains germinal , rfd4_proteina and a refold-enabled rfd case, since the two workflows the regression reached had no compilation test at all. boltz_pae_mean was always blank while every other engine filled <tool>_pae_mean . Boltz's confidence JSON carries no PAE of any kind, but it does write the full matrix as pae_*.npz , already read for ipSAE; bin/parse_boltz_confidence.py --pae-npz now takes the mean off it in the same step, so the column is filled from the same numbers ipSAE is computed from. BindCraft reporting failed to render against matplotlib 3.11. Axes.boxplot 's labels keyword became tick_labels in 3.9 and is gone in 3.11, and the report has to run against whatever matplotlib the BindCraft image carries; it now picks the keyword from the signature once and uses it for all thirteen boxplots. Two fold runs in one workflow wrote their per-engine score tables to the same path, so the second overwrote the first and the merge downstream saw rows for complexes it never folded. The fold stack now takes a publish label ( FOLD , FOLD_PREDICT and each engine subworkflow), which the refold uses to keep the complex folds and the binder-monomer folds apart. bin/rmsd4all.py compared multi-chain structures in file order rather than in the order the --superimpose-chains / --score-chains lists gave, and rmsd_all pairs atoms by position. Two complexes holding the same chains but written in the opposite order - an RFD4-Proteina design, which writes the binder first, against a refold that writes the target first - had the binder measured against the target: 21 Å where the structures agree to 1.3 Å. The chains are now taken in the order asked for, which is what makes the two lists a statement of correspondence. BindCraft interface scoring of a Boltz-refolded complex was given the design's binder chain id, but the refolded complex has its own chain ids (binder A, target B). Wherever the design's binder was not chain A - --method rfd4_proteina , where it is B - every interface metric, and the sequence column beside them, described the target rather than the binder. rfd4_proteina: --rfd4_target_chain / --rfd4_binder_chain resolved to the literal string "false" when left unset, because the params default to boolean false and false.toString() is a non-empty, therefore truthy, string. The A/B default and the derivation from --contigs never ran, so filter metrics were computed on a chain that does not exist - every rg blank and every design rejected - and the binder sequence was read from the wrong chain. rfd4_proteina: the boltz_monomer_vs_complex_rmsd_* columns in combined_scores.tsv were always empty. The merge stripped _model_0.pdb / _monomer from the RMSD table's structure1 , but the values there end in _complex.pdb , so the key never matched a design id. --boltz_num_workers (default: task.cpus , unchanged): Boltz's dataloader workers deadlock on some platforms, leaving the run at 0% GPU indefinitely rather than failing. conf/platforms/arm64.config sets it to 0. Previously --num_workers was hardcoded to task.cpus in three modules and could not be overridden, since a duplicate flag in ext.args does not win. rfd4_proteina: COMBINE_RFD4_SCORES failed with Not a valid path value type whenever the filters rejected every design, because the empty-channel fallback passed Channel.of(file(...)) to ifEmpty , which takes a value rather than a channel. RF3 wrote its caches to $HOME , which is / when the container runs as a uid with no passwd entry - what conf/platforms/arm64.config asks for under Docker so a task can write its own work directory. rf3 fold died with PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/.cache' before any folding. RF3_FOLD and ROSETTAFOLD3 now set XDG_CACHE_HOME , XDG_CONFIG_HOME and TRITON_CACHE_DIR inside the task directory, as the Boltz module already did. rfd3: treat unset/ false --rf3_batch_size as 1 (avoids Boolean→Integer cast failure when a shared config sentinel is present). The GPU lock ( --gpu_devices ) failed whenever the tasks sharing it did not all run as the same user. Some images run as root and others are pinned to the invoking user ( conf/platforms/arm64.config does this under Docker), and the lock files take the ownership of whichever task created them, so a task running as anyone else could not open one for writing and waited out --gpu_lock_timeout before failing. bin/gpu_lock.sh now creates the lock directory and its files world-writable, and a lock file it cannot write is reported once and fails the task immediately rather than being waited on. The GPU trace directory is created the same way; a trace row written by a task running as another user was previously dropped in silence. A lock directory left behind by an earlier run has to be deleted for the new permissions to take effect. examples/pdl1-rfd/run-m3-full.sh and examples/pdl1-bindcraft/run-m3.sh : point at repo main.nf , pin NXF_VER=24.10.0 , and drop mid-command # comments that broke the Nextflow invocation. Root nextflow.config report/trace timestamps use params.trace_timestamp instead of a top-level def , so Nextflow >=26 can parse the root config. Remove unused random_choice helper from conf/platforms/m3.config . Quarto reports: set writable XDG_* / Jupyter runtime dirs so rendering works in Apptainer (was failing with Could create runtime directory for jupyter transport ). Local multi-GPU runs no longer stack tasks on one card while another sits idle ( #14 ). docs workflow: main , develop and tag pushes no longer race each other deploying to gh-pages . A release triggered all three at once and two failed with cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/gh-pages' , so the versioned docs were never published. Runs are now serialised and a rejected push is retried.
