docs.text: Refold Scoring ( --refold_with ) Refolding provides independent structural validation for designs previously predicted during generation. Every design workflow evaluates its generated backbones before this stage: AlphaFold2 initial guess in --method rfd and --method rfd_partial , RosettaFold3 in --method rfd3 , and native AF2 prediction passes in BindCraft and Germinal. Refolding does not replace those initial evaluations. Instead, it takes selected designs, co-folds each binder sequence against the target using independent prediction engines, compares predicted conformations to the designed pose, and re-scores the interface. Initial prediction scores determine which candidates are selected for refolding. Refold scoring is available across six design workflows: rfd , rfd_partial , rfd3 , rfd4_proteina , bindcraft , and germinal . Each workflow accepts the same --refold_* parameters and appends engine-prefixed score columns to its combined_scores.tsv . Refolding is disabled by default because it requires additional GPU compute per candidate design. The subworkflow is implemented in subworkflows/local/refold.nf and subworkflows/local/refold_select.nf , with shared defaults defined in conf/refold.config and conf/refold_fold_stack.config . Prediction engines Specify engines as a comma-separated list: --refold_with boltz,chai1,openfold3 All engines supported by --method fold are available: af2 , af2_mono , boltz , rf3 , protenix , af3 , openfold3 , chai1 , esmfold2 , and esmfold2_fast . Candidate selection Three parameters govern candidate selection and can be combined. When none are set, all designs are refolded: Parameter Default Description --refold_filter none Threshold filter applied to initial scores, semicolon-separated (e.g. 'ipsae>=0.5;pae_interaction<=10' ). Uses the same syntax as --rfd_filters . --refold_sort_by none Metric used to rank candidates passing the filter; prefix with - for descending order. --refold_max none Maximum number of designs to refold. Filtering and batching behaviour: Streaming evaluation with --refold_filter : filters evaluate per design. A candidate is submitted for refolding as soon as its initial scores are available, without waiting for the remaining set. Global evaluation with --refold_max : capping the number of refolded designs requires evaluating the full candidate set before dispatching refold jobs, because ranking requires global comparison. Ranking with --refold_max and --refold_sort_by : the pipeline selects the top N designs according to the specified metric. If --refold_max is specified without --refold_sort_by , designs are selected in completion order, and the pipeline emits a warning. Sorting without --refold_max : specifying --refold_sort_by without --refold_max does not filter designs. All candidates passing the filter are refolded, and the pipeline emits a warning. If a filter references a column missing from the score table, the pipeline terminates with an error listing available columns rather than excluding all designs without explanation. Specify --refold_sort_by with an = Use --refold_sort_by='-ipsae' , not --refold_sort_by '-ipsae' . Without the = , Nextflow interprets the leading hyphen as a Nextflow CLI option. Metrics where lower values are preferred ( pae_interaction , pair_pae_min , RMSD) require no prefix. Selection report All candidate designs evaluated for refolding are logged in <refold_publish_dir>/refold_selection.tsv : Column Description design_id Design identifier refold_selection selected or rejected refold_rank Rank position when --refold_max is set (ranked by --refold_sort_by , or arrival order without it) refold_sort_metric Metric used for ranking refold_sort_value Metric value for that design Modifying selection parameters on resume requires a new --outdir refold_scores.tsv , refold_rmsd.tsv , and refold_selection.tsv are gathered using collectFile(storeDir:) . Rerunning with modified selection parameters into an existing output directory retains previously gathered TSV files, causing mismatched reports. When changing selection criteria, specify a new --outdir . Binder chain identification --refold_binder_chain and --refold_target_chain apply specifically to --method bindcraft and --method germinal (defaults: binder B , target A ). rfd3 and rfd4_proteina infer chains from contig specifications, whereas rfd and rfd_partial identify chains from AF2 initial guess complexes. Target sequence configuration By default, the refold target sequence matches the target from design generation: the target chain sequence is parsed from selected design structures, and the consensus sequence across designs is used for refolding. When designs report divergent target sequences, the pipeline logs a warning and uses the most frequent sequence. --refold_target_fasta supplies an alternate target sequence: --refold_target_fasta full_length_target.fasta This option allows testing binders against full-length targets when initial designs were generated against truncated domains, assessing whether binding geometry is maintained in the complete protein context. The FASTA file must contain exactly one record . Because each binder is folded against the target and scores are recorded one row per design in refold_scores.tsv , evaluating multiple target variants requires separate pipeline executions with distinct --outdir locations. The pipeline verifies that the target sequence from the design structures appears as a subsequence within the provided FASTA. If not found, a warning is logged. Target structures and MSAs Three fold-stack parameters configure target inputs: Parameter Description --templates Template structures matched to folded chains by sequence. Providing a full-length target structure enables prediction engines to model regions omitted during initial design. Only the target chain is templated unless --binder_templates is set. --target_msa Precomputed A3M alignment for the target. The first record must match the target sequence. Mutually exclusive with --create_target_msa . --create_target_msa Generates a target MSA using --msa_method alongside --use_msa_server , --colabfold_envdb , or --uniref30 . These parameters omit the --refold_ prefix because fold stack operations during design workflows pertain exclusively to refolding. Full-complex RMSD columns require equal sequence lengths When --refold_target_fasta provides a target longer than the design structure, whole-complex alignment metrics requiring identical residue counts ( <tool>_complex_rmsd_all and <tool>_complex_tm_score_all ) evaluate to NaN . Structurally aligned pruned variants and target-aligned binder RMSD ( <tool>_target_aligned_binder_rmsd_* ) remain valid because the binder chain length is unchanged. The DockQ columns likewise remain valid: residues are paired by sequence alignment and each pair contributes the atoms both structures carry, so a longer target simply contributes the part it shares with the design. DockQ's receptor and ligand are the target and the binder --refold_target_chain is the receptor and --refold_binder_chain the ligand, where the reference DockQ implementation instead always takes the larger chain as the receptor. fnat and iRMSD are symmetric and agree either way; LRMSD , and so the DockQ score, differ when the binder is the larger of the two. Requires nf-binder-design-utils:0.1.8 or later, which carries peppr . Output columns Prediction engines generate standardized columns in combined_scores.tsv , prefixed with the engine name: Column Description <tool>_iptm_max , <tool>_ipsae_max , <tool>_plddt_max , ... Prediction confidence metrics, per --refold_metrics <tool>_target_aligned_binder_rmsd_all Binder RMSD relative to the design pose after superimposing on the target <tool>_target_aligned_binder_dockq DockQ of the refolded complex against the design pose, 0 to 1. The usual reading is <0.23 incorrect, 0.23-0.49 acceptable, 0.49-0.80 medium, >=0.80 high <tool>_target_aligned_binder_dockq_fnat , _dockq_fnonnat , _dockq_irmsd , _dockq_lrmsd The components DockQ is built from: fraction of design contacts recovered, fraction of predicted contacts that are not in the design, interface backbone RMSD and ligand (binder) RMSD <tool>_target_aligned_binder_interface_lddt Interface lDDT of the refolded complex against the design <tool>_target_aligned_binder_clash_count Atom clashes within the refolded complex. A property of the prediction alone, not a comparison <tool>_complex_rmsd_all Whole-complex RMSD relative to the design <tool>_monomer_vs_design_rmsd_all RMSD of binder folded alone versus its designed conformation <tool>_monomer_vs_complex_rmsd_all RMSD of binder folded alone versus binder in the refolded complex <tool>_interface_dG , <tool>_interface_dSASA , ... BindCraft interface metrics evaluated on the refolded complex <tool>_selected_batch , <tool>_selected_model Sample identifier corresponding to the reported RMSD and interface metrics consensus_z , n_tools Cross-engine consensus z-score and count of contributing tools, prioritizing designs supported by multiple independent predictors refold_sample_scores.tsv , published in the same directory, records individual sample predictions (keyed by id , tool , batch , model ) without aggregation, enabling custom post-processing. Reporting parameters Parameter Default Description --refold_with none Comma-separated list of prediction engines --refold_metrics iptm/ipsae/plddt/ptm/pae Summary metrics included in combined_scores.tsv --refold_structure_stat selected Method for aggregating structural metrics across samples: selected , min , first , mean , or max --refold_binder_monomer true Folds each binder alone for monomer-versus-complex and monomer-versus-design RMSD comparisons --refold_monomer_single_sequence true Predicts binder monomer structures from sequence alone without MSA generation --refold_interface_scoring true Calculates BindCraft interface metrics on refolded complexes --refold_dockq true Calculates DockQ, its components, interface lDDT and a clash count for the target-aligned binder comparison --output_rmsd_aligned false Saves superimposed coordinate files from RMSD comparisons --n_predictions 5 Generated structures per design per engine With --refold_structure_stat selected , RMSD and interface metrics are extracted from the top-ranked sample (ranked by --consensus_metric , default ipSAE) rather than aggregated across samples independently. Because structural metrics describe a specific molecular conformation, taking independent minimums across different metrics would produce inconsistent composite values. Setting min , mean , max , or first applies that statistical operator across all structural columns. Fold stack configuration Refolding uses the same underlying prediction pipeline as --method fold and --method fold_pulldown . Alignment and template configurations derive from standard fold stack parameters: --msa_method , --create_target_msa , --target_msa , --use_msa_server , --templates , --colabfold_envdb , and --uniref30 . Prediction engine flags ( --af2_* , --boltz_* , --protenix_* , --af3_* , --openfold3_* , --chai1_* , --esmfold2_* ) apply as documented under --method fold . RosettaFold3 requires specific refold parameter prefixes to distinguish them from generation-time parameters in --method rfd3 : --refold_rf3_ckpt_path , --refold_rf3_num_steps , --refold_rf3_n_recycles , --refold_rf3_batch_size , --refold_rf3_early_stopping_plddt_threshold , and --refold_rf3_seed . When declared, the fold stack reads these prefixed parameters. Renamed and deprecated parameters Parameters previously prefixed with --full_refold_* have been renamed to --refold_* ( --full_refold_with is --refold_with , --full_refold_max is --refold_max , and --full_refold_filter_sort is --refold_sort_by ). Deprecated parameters accepted with a warning: Deprecated Replacement --refold_af2ig_filters --refold_filter --refold_oracles --refold_with --refold_oracles_max --refold_max Removed parameters (alignment and template options now use fold stack parameters directly): Removed Replacement --refold_create_target_msa --create_target_msa --refold_use_msa_server --use_msa_server --refold_target_templates --templates --refold_alignment --target_msa --refold_target_fasta remains under its own name because target sequence substitution is unique to refolding (see Target sequence configuration ). --boltz_refold_batch_size has been removed. Use --refold_boltz_batch_size to configure sample batching per job. See also RFdiffusion Workflows RFdiffusion3 Workflow RFD4-Proteina Workflow Fold Workflow : details on prediction engine flags

docs.text: BindCraft2 Workflow Parallel BindCraft2 execution for protein binder design across multiple GPUs. BindCraft2 cannot be offered as a hosted service BindCraft2 is under a source-available, hosting-restricted license . It is free to use for any purpose, including commercial use, on your own or your organisation's infrastructure, and you may share the designs it produces. However, you may not provide BindCraft2, or a service whose functionality derives from it, to third parties as a hosted, cloud, API, web application, workflow platform or SaaS offering without a separate commercial license from the copyright holders. This restriction carries through to nf-binder-design : the --method bc2 workflow must not be deployed as a hosted service (or as an invocable tool or workflow step in a hosted platform) for third parties. Overview The --method bc2 workflow (alias --method bindcraft2 ) runs BindCraft2 campaigns in parallel batches, then gathers them with bindcraft campaign_output and renders an HTML report. BindCraft2 is a rewrite of BindCraft , not a version bump. It runs as a separate --method bc2 workflow instead of a flag on --method bindcraft , adding: One campaign JSON instead of three settings files; set any option from the CLI via --bc2_set . Twelve binder modalities ( VHH , scFv , Fab , ARP , cyclic_peptide , multidomain , induced_fit , ...) and nine composable design properties ( --bc2_humanize , --bc2_protease_stable , ...). Multi-target campaigns, off-target detargeting, and PDB, mmCIF or FASTA inputs. mmCIF structure output and i_pDAE candidate ranking. Differences from standalone BindCraft2 Standalone BindCraft2 runs on a single GPU until it produces N accepted designs. This pipeline: Runs a fixed trajectory budget ( --bc2_n_traj ), split into batches of --bc2_batch_size Exits once the budget finishes, keeping runtime predictable Parallelises batches across available GPUs Assigns a distinct campaign_seed per batch to prevent duplicate trajectories To target a specific count of accepted designs, start with a small budget ( --bc2_n_traj 100 ) to measure the acceptance rate, then scale --bc2_n_traj . Adaptive tuning under batching BindCraft2 includes two adaptive mechanisms that update settings mid-campaign based on the current campaign's trajectory table: Mechanism Engages after autotune every 10 trajectories in one campaign desperation 750 fruitless trajectories in one campaign, then one escalation rung per 50 Each batch executes --bc2_batch_size trajectories, so both mechanisms remain inactive at the default batch size of 1. That suits fixed-budget, reproducible comparisons, though long standalone runs on difficult targets behave differently once adaptive tuning activates. The pipeline logs inactive mechanisms with the batch plan. Increase --bc2_batch_size if you want autotune to activate. Command-line Options See available options with --method bc2 --help : nextflow run Australian-Protein-Design-Initiative/nf-binder-design \ --method bc2 --help Example Usage Params mode Generate the campaign JSON from flat parameters, using the same parameter names as --method bindcraft : #!/bin/bash nextflow run Australian-Protein-Design-Initiative/nf-binder-design \ --method bc2 \ --input_pdb 'input/PDL1.pdb' \ --outdir results \ --target_chains "A" \ --hotspot_res "A56,A125" \ --binder_length_range "60-150" \ --bc2_n_traj 8 \ --bc2_batch_size 2 \ -profile local \ -resume Config mode Pass a BindCraft2 campaign JSON directly. Nextflow detects referenced files ( targets[].target_path and binder_scaffold ), stages them into each task, and rewrites their paths so relative entries resolve from any launch directory: nextflow run Australian-Protein-Design-Initiative/nf-binder-design \ --method bc2 \ --bc2_config campaign.json \ --bc2_modality VHH \ --bc2_humanize \ --bc2_n_traj 100 \ --bc2_batch_size 5 \ -profile local Built-in target presets BindCraft2 includes preconfigured targets inside the container. Setting "target" in the campaign JSON loads the target structure, chains and hotspots from the container without staging external files: { "campaign_name": "hPDL1_VHH", "target": "hPDL1", "modality": "VHH", "humanize": true } Available presets: hPDL1 , mPDL1 , hPD1 , hIL2R , hIL7RA and dynorphin_a . Run bindcraft design --list-targets inside the container to list current presets. Modality and design properties are standard campaign JSON keys, so you can set them in JSON instead of passing --bc2_modality or --bc2_* CLI flags. For running on SLURM, use -profile slurm with --slurm_account=xxYY and the appropriate -c site-specific configuration file (refer to and adapt from the rfdiffusion example ). Key Parameters Flag Description --bc2_config BindCraft2 campaign settings JSON. Mutually exclusive with --input_pdb --input_pdb Target PDB, mmCIF or FASTA; a directory or quoted glob runs each structure. Mutually exclusive with --bc2_config --target_chains Target chain IDs, comma-separated (params mode) --hotspot_res Hotspot residues, e.g. A54,A56 or B12-16 (params mode) --hotspot_subsample Fraction of each target's hotspots to keep per batch (both modes) --binder_length_range 60-150 range, 80 exact, or 60,80,100 discrete choices (params mode) --bc2_n_traj Total trajectories to run --bc2_batch_size Trajectories per parallel task --bc2_seed Base campaign_seed . Batch seed is bc2_seed + seedIndex ( seedIndex is the batch index in config mode, or pdbIndex * nBatches + batchIndex for several structures in params mode) --gpu_devices Specify multiple GPUs, e.g. --gpu_devices=0,1 (use only for -profile local ) --do_foldseek Run a FoldSeek structural novelty search over the ranked designs Hotspot subsampling --hotspot_subsample samples ceil(N * fraction) hotspots per target (minimum 1) independently for each batch, so batches explore different parts of the epitope. --hotspot_res "A54,A56,A66,A115" --hotspot_subsample 0.5 With these flags, each batch selects two of the four hotspots using its campaign_seed . Sampling uses --bc2_seed for reproducibility; --method bindcraft seeds hotspot subsampling from the system clock instead. Subsampling behaviour: Works in both params and config mode, since subsampling runs while staging the campaign JSON into each task. Treats each comma-separated entry as one hotspot, keeping or dropping ranges like B12-16 as a unit. Samples each target independently in multi-target campaigns. Applies only to hotspots defined under targets[] in the campaign JSON. Hotspots from a built-in "target" preset are merged by BindCraft2 after staging and are not subsampled; the pipeline logs a warning if you combine --hotspot_subsample with a preset target. Passing BindCraft2 Settings --bc2_set BindCraft2 exposes around 235 settings. Pass any of them via --bc2_set as KEY=VALUE pairs forwarded to bindcraft design --set : --bc2_set 'binder_lengths=[70,90];filters.i_pTM.threshold=0.8;design_models=3' Separate assignments with ; instead of , , because JSON values often contain commas. Dotted keys update nested fields: filters.i_pTM.threshold=0.8 changes only that threshold. Values parse as JSON (falling back to plain strings), so [70,90] becomes a list and humanize=true becomes a boolean. Full setting list: settings/core/reference.json . docs.text: The --method bc2 workflow (alias --method bindcraft2 ) runs BindCraft2 campaigns in parallel batches, then gathers them with bindcraft campaign_output and renders an HTML report. BindCraft2 is a rewrite of BindCraft , not a version bump. It runs as a separate --method bc2 workflow instead of a flag on --method bindcraft , adding: One campaign JSON instead of three settings files; set any option from the CLI via --bc2_set . Twelve binder modalities ( VHH , scFv , Fab , ARP , cyclic_peptide , multidomain , induced_fit , ...) and nine composable design properties ( --bc2_humanize , --bc2_protease_stable , ...). Multi-target campaigns, off-target detargeting, and PDB, mmCIF or FASTA inputs. mmCIF structure output and i_pDAE candidate ranking.
docs.title: Overview

docs.text: Standalone BindCraft2 runs on a single GPU until it produces N accepted designs. This pipeline: Runs a fixed trajectory budget ( --bc2_n_traj ), split into batches of --bc2_batch_size Exits once the budget finishes, keeping runtime predictable Parallelises batches across available GPUs Assigns a distinct campaign_seed per batch to prevent duplicate trajectories To target a specific count of accepted designs, start with a small budget ( --bc2_n_traj 100 ) to measure the acceptance rate, then scale --bc2_n_traj .
docs.title: Differences from standalone BindCraft2

docs.text: BindCraft2 includes two adaptive mechanisms that update settings mid-campaign based on the current campaign's trajectory table: Mechanism Engages after autotune every 10 trajectories in one campaign desperation 750 fruitless trajectories in one campaign, then one escalation rung per 50 Each batch executes --bc2_batch_size trajectories, so both mechanisms remain inactive at the default batch size of 1. That suits fixed-budget, reproducible comparisons, though long standalone runs on difficult targets behave differently once adaptive tuning activates. The pipeline logs inactive mechanisms with the batch plan. Increase --bc2_batch_size if you want autotune to activate.
docs.title: Adaptive tuning under batching

docs.text: --hotspot_subsample samples ceil(N * fraction) hotspots per target (minimum 1) independently for each batch, so batches explore different parts of the epitope. --hotspot_res "A54,A56,A66,A115" --hotspot_subsample 0.5 With these flags, each batch selects two of the four hotspots using its campaign_seed . Sampling uses --bc2_seed for reproducibility; --method bindcraft seeds hotspot subsampling from the system clock instead. Subsampling behaviour: Works in both params and config mode, since subsampling runs while staging the campaign JSON into each task. Treats each comma-separated entry as one hotspot, keeping or dropping ranges like B12-16 as a unit. Samples each target independently in multi-target campaigns. Applies only to hotspots defined under targets[] in the campaign JSON. Hotspots from a built-in "target" preset are merged by BindCraft2 after staging and are not subsampled; the pipeline logs a warning if you combine --hotspot_subsample with a preset target.

docs.text: BindCraft Workflow Parallel BindCraft execution for protein binder design across multiple GPUs. Overview The --method bindcraft workflow runs BindCraft trajectories in parallel across multiple GPUs - ideal for HPC clusters or multi-GPU workstations. Key Differences Unlike a 'vanilla' BindCraft run which runs on a single GPU indefinitely until finding N accepted designs, this pipeline: Runs a fixed number of relaxed trajectories ( --bindcraft_n_traj per input PDB) Stops when complete (predictable runtime) Parallelizes across available GPUs Outputs an HTML summary report --input_pdb accepts a single file, a directory of PDB files, or a quoted glob (e.g. 'input/*.pdb' ). Shared settings ( --target_chains , --hotspot_res , --contigs ) apply to every input PDB. Batch directories and design names use <pdbName>_<batchIndex> (e.g. batches/PDL1_0/ ). Merged stats CSVs ( final_design_stats.csv , trajectory_stats.csv , mpnn_design_stats.csv ) include a Target column with the input structure filename including extension (e.g. PDL1.pdb ) so multi-PDB runs can be compared; the HTML report displays Target without the extension. If you want to generate a specific number of accepted designs, we suggest running a small number of trajectories ( --bindcraft_n_traj 100 or --bindcraft_n_traj 300 ) to assess the acceptance rate, then knowing the ratio of accepted designs to total trajectories, do a larger run to generate (approximately) the desired number of accepted designs. The HTML report headline accept rate collapses MPNN duplicates (multiple accepted sequences from the same trajectory count once); the rate including all accepted MPNN sequences is shown as well. Multi-PDB runs also get per-target accept rates and metric comparisons. Command-line Options See available options with --method bindcraft --help : nextflow run Australian-Protein-Design-Initiative/nf-binder-design \ --method bindcraft --help Example Usage #!/bin/bash nextflow run Australian-Protein-Design-Initiative/nf-binder-design \ --method bindcraft \ --input_pdb 'input/PDL1.pdb' \ --outdir results \ --target_chains "A" \ --hotspot_res "A56,A125" \ --hotspot_subsample 0.5 \ --binder_length_range "55-120" \ --bindcraft_n_traj 2 \ --bindcraft_batch_size 1 \ --bindcraft_advanced_settings_preset "default_4stage_multimer" \ --bindcraft_filters_preset "default_filters" \ -profile local \ -resume For running on SLURM, you can use the -profile slurm flag instead of -profile local , with --slurm_account=xxYY and the appropriate -c site-specific configuration file (refer to and adapt from the rfdiffusion example ). Key Parameters Flag Description --input_pdb Target PDB file, directory of PDBs, or quoted glob (e.g. 'input/*.pdb' ). --bindcraft_n_traj is run per input PDB --target_chains Target chain IDs (comma-separated) --hotspot_res Hotspot residues (comma-separated) --hotspot_subsample Random proportion of hotspot residues per design (explores hotspot selection) --binder_length_range Range of binder lengths to design --bindcraft_n_traj Number of trajectories to run per input PDB --bindcraft_batch_size Number of trajectories per batch --gpu_devices Specify multiple GPUs, e.g., --gpu_devices=0,1 (use only for -profile local ) BindCraft Presets Advanced Settings Presets Flag Description --bindcraft_advanced_settings_preset Use a preset from settings_advanced (without .json extension) Keep in mind, the experimental success rate of the advanced presets may not have been as rigorously validated as the default4stage_multimer preset. Caveat emptor. Filter Presets Flag Description --bindcraft_filters_preset Use filter settings presets from settings_filters (without .json extension). In most cases, it's probably best to stick with the default. Output Structure Results are saved to --outdir in the bindcraft/ subdirectory: ── bindcraft │ ├── accepted │ │ └── results │ │ └── Accepted │ │ ├── bindcraft_design_1_l57_s942028_mpnn6_model1.pdb │ │ └── bindcraft_design_1_l57_s942028_mpnn8_model2.pdb │ ├── batches │ │ ├── PDL1_0 │ │ │ └── results │ │ │ ├── failure_csv.csv │ │ │ ├── final_design_stats.csv │ │ │ ├── mpnn_design_stats.csv │ │ │ ├── Trajectory │ │ │ └── trajectory_stats.csv │ │ └── PDL1_1 │ │ └── results │ │ ├── Accepted │ │ ├── failure_csv.csv │ │ ├── final_design_stats.csv │ │ ├── MPNN │ │ ├── mpnn_design_stats.csv │ │ ├── Rejected │ │ ├── Trajectory │ │ └── trajectory_stats.csv │ ├── bindcraft_report.html │ ├── failure_csv.csv │ ├── final_design_stats.csv │ ├── mpnn_design_stats.csv │ └── trajectory_stats.csv └── logs ├── dag_20250725_084959.html ├── report_20250725_084959.html ├── timeline_20250725_084959.html ├── trace_20250725_084959.txt A summary report is generated as bindcraft_report.html . Refold Scoring (Optional) BindCraft runs its own AF2 passes and gates designs on their scores, which determines which candidates reach accepted/ . --refold_with provides independent validation: accepted designs are folded again with one or more external predictors, compared with the design pose, and interface metrics are re-scored. nextflow run main.nf --method bindcraft \ --input_pdb 'input/PDL1.pdb' --target_chains "A" --hotspot_res "A56,A125" \ --refold_with boltz \ --refold_max 50 \ --use_msa_server This is the shared refold scoring step, with the same --refold_filter , --refold_sort_by and --refold_max selection parameters as other design workflows. The gate and ranking read BindCraft's final_design_stats.csv columns. BindCraft has no chain derivation of its own, so --refold_binder_chain (default B ) and --refold_target_chain (default A ) name the chains if yours differ. Outputs are saved under bindcraft/refold/ . FoldSeek Structural Search (Optional) After BindCraft completes, you can optionally run FoldSeek structural similarity search on accepted designs. The binder chain is automatically extracted from each accepted complex: only the binder is searched, not the full target–binder complex. FoldSeek summary results are output to {outdir}/foldseek/{database_name}/ . See FoldSeek output format for details. Enabling FoldSeek Add --do_foldseek to your bindcraft command: nextflow run main.nf --method bindcraft \ --input_pdb target.pdb --target_chains A \ --do_foldseek FoldSeek Flags Flag Default Description --do_foldseek false Enable FoldSeek search on accepted designs All common --foldseek_* flags (database, search mode, output options, CATH annotation) are documented in the FoldSeek subworkflow docs . Examples The examples/ directory contains complete working examples for BindCraft workflows: examples/pdl1-bindcraft : PDL1 binder example from the BindCraft repository examples/egfr-bindcraft : an EGFR binder design example examples/mdm2-bindcraft-peptide - peptide binder design for MDM2, based on Filus et al, 2025 See the examples/README.md for details.

docs.text: #!/bin/bash nextflow run Australian-Protein-Design-Initiative/nf-binder-design \ --method bindcraft \ --input_pdb 'input/PDL1.pdb' \ --outdir results \ --target_chains "A" \ --hotspot_res "A56,A125" \ --hotspot_subsample 0.5 \ --binder_length_range "55-120" \ --bindcraft_n_traj 2 \ --bindcraft_batch_size 1 \ --bindcraft_advanced_settings_preset "default_4stage_multimer" \ --bindcraft_filters_preset "default_filters" \ -profile local \ -resume For running on SLURM, you can use the -profile slurm flag instead of -profile local , with --slurm_account=xxYY and the appropriate -c site-specific configuration file (refer to and adapt from the rfdiffusion example ).
docs.title: Example Usage

docs.text: Flag Description --input_pdb Target PDB file, directory of PDBs, or quoted glob (e.g. 'input/*.pdb' ). --bindcraft_n_traj is run per input PDB --target_chains Target chain IDs (comma-separated) --hotspot_res Hotspot residues (comma-separated) --hotspot_subsample Random proportion of hotspot residues per design (explores hotspot selection) --binder_length_range Range of binder lengths to design --bindcraft_n_traj Number of trajectories to run per input PDB --bindcraft_batch_size Number of trajectories per batch --gpu_devices Specify multiple GPUs, e.g., --gpu_devices=0,1 (use only for -profile local )

docs.text: Flag Description --bindcraft_advanced_settings_preset Use a preset from settings_advanced (without .json extension) Keep in mind, the experimental success rate of the advanced presets may not have been as rigorously validated as the default4stage_multimer preset. Caveat emptor.
docs.title: Advanced Settings Presets

docs.text: Flag Description --bindcraft_filters_preset Use filter settings presets from settings_filters (without .json extension). In most cases, it's probably best to stick with the default.

docs.text: BindCraft runs its own AF2 passes and gates designs on their scores, which determines which candidates reach accepted/ . --refold_with provides independent validation: accepted designs are folded again with one or more external predictors, compared with the design pose, and interface metrics are re-scored. nextflow run main.nf --method bindcraft \ --input_pdb 'input/PDL1.pdb' --target_chains "A" --hotspot_res "A56,A125" \ --refold_with boltz \ --refold_max 50 \ --use_msa_server This is the shared refold scoring step, with the same --refold_filter , --refold_sort_by and --refold_max selection parameters as other design workflows. The gate and ranking read BindCraft's final_design_stats.csv columns. BindCraft has no chain derivation of its own, so --refold_binder_chain (default B ) and --refold_target_chain (default A ) name the chains if yours differ. Outputs are saved under bindcraft/refold/ .
docs.title: Refold Scoring (Optional)

docs.text: After BindCraft completes, you can optionally run FoldSeek structural similarity search on accepted designs. The binder chain is automatically extracted from each accepted complex: only the binder is searched, not the full target–binder complex. FoldSeek summary results are output to {outdir}/foldseek/{database_name}/ . See FoldSeek output format for details.
docs.title: FoldSeek Structural Search (Optional)

docs.text: Add --do_foldseek to your bindcraft command: nextflow run main.nf --method bindcraft \ --input_pdb target.pdb --target_chains A \ --do_foldseek
docs.title: Enabling FoldSeek

docs.text: Flag Default Description --do_foldseek false Enable FoldSeek search on accepted designs All common --foldseek_* flags (database, search mode, output options, CATH annotation) are documented in the FoldSeek subworkflow docs .

docs.text: BoltzGen Workflow The --method boltzgen workflow automates the design of binders using the BoltzGen generative model. The key advantage of this workflow is improved parallelization across multiple GPUs and better resource allocation on HPC clusters. It supports the protein-anything , peptide-anything , protein_small-molecule and nanobody-anything protocols. Overview The BoltzGen workflow performs the following steps, as per boltzgen run : Design : Generates binder backbone structures based on a YAML configuration. Inverse Folding : Generates sequences for the designed backbones. Folding : Re-folds the designed binder in complex with the target. Design Folding : Re-folds the designed binder alone. Affinity : (Optional - protein_small-molecule protocol only) Calculates affinity scores for protein-small molecule complexes. ( Merge batches : nf-binder-design --method boltzgen merges independently generated batches of designs, ready for analysis and filtering) Analysis & Filtering : Aggregates scores and filters designs based on user-defined criteria. General Information Command-line Options You can see available options with --method boltzgen --help : nextflow run Australian-Protein-Design-Initiative/nf-binder-design \ --method boltzgen --help YAML Configuration The BoltzGen workflow is controlled by a YAML configuration file passed via --config_yaml . This file defines the input structure, constraints, and design objectives. Refer to the BoltzGen documentation on how to prepare your configuration file. Note: ⚠️ BoltzGen expects residues specified as indices starting at 1, irresepctive of the numbering in your PDB/mmCIF file. You may find it easier to use bin/renumber_chains.py to renumber your input PDB to be sequentially numbered starting at 1 to simplify choosing hotspot residues in ChimeraX/Pymol/Molstar etc. Usage Basic Execution To run the workflow with a configuration file: nextflow run Australian-Protein-Design-Initiative/nf-binder-design \ --method boltzgen \ --config_yaml config/my_design.yaml Key Parameters Flag Default Description --config_yaml (required) Path to the BoltzGen YAML configuration file --outdir results Output directory for results --design_name config basename Name of the design, used for output file prefixes --protocol protein-anything Protocol type: protein-anything , peptide-anything , protein-small_molecule , or nanobody-anything --num_designs 100 Total number of designs to generate --inverse_fold_num_sequences 1 Number of sequences to generate per backbone during inverse folding --batch_size 10 Number of designs to process per batch --budget 10 Final number of designs to keep after diversity optimization and filtering --devices 1 Number of GPU devices to use --num_workers Number of DataLoader workers Filtering Parameters Flag Default Description --alpha Trade-off for sequence diversity selection: 0.0=quality-only, 1.0=diversity-only --filter_biased true Remove amino-acid composition outliers (use --filter_biased false to disable) --metrics_override Per-metric inverse-importance weights for ranking. Format: metric_name=weight (e.g., 'plip_hbonds_refolded=4' 'delta_sasa_refolded=2' ) --additional_filters Extra hard filters. Format: feature>threshold or feature<threshold (e.g., 'design_ALA>0.3' 'design_GLY<0.2' ) --size_buckets Constraint for maximum designs in size ranges. Format: min-max:count (e.g., '10-20:5' '20-30:10' ) --refolding_rmsd_threshold Threshold used for RMSD-based filters (lower is better) Key Outputs The results directory (or specified --outdir ) will contain: params.json : A record of the parameters used for the run. boltzgen/batches : Each independent design batch, in folders for each step ( design , inverse_folding , folding , design_folding ) bolzgen/merged : All batches merged, after the 'analysis' step. boltzgen/filtered : Final designs are in filtered/final_ranked_designs after the 'filtering' step. boltzgen/merged should be equivalent to the output of a non-Nextflow execution of boltzgen run - see the BoltzGen docs for details on the pipeline output . Re-running Filtering Use boltzgen_filter.nf to re-run filtering on existing results with different parameters: nextflow run boltzgen_filter.nf --run results/boltzgen/merged --budget 20 --alpha 0.05 The --config_yaml and --protocol are auto-detected from params.json if not specified. All filtering parameters from the main workflow are available. Results are saved to results/boltzgen/filtered/final_ranked_designs/ . FoldSeek Structural Search (Optional) After filtering, you can optionally run FoldSeek structural similarity search on the final designs. The design (shorter/binder) chain is automatically extracted from each complex mmCIF: only the binder is searched, not the full target–binder complex. FoldSeek summary results are output to {outdir}/foldseek/{database_name}/ . See FoldSeek output format for details. Enabling FoldSeek Add --do_foldseek to your boltzgen command: nextflow run Australian-Protein-Design-Initiative/nf-binder-design \ --method boltzgen \ --config_yaml config/my_design.yaml \ --do_foldseek FoldSeek Flags Flag Default Description --do_foldseek false Enable FoldSeek search on final designs All common --foldseek_* flags (database, search mode, output options, CATH annotation) are documented in the FoldSeek subworkflow docs . Examples The examples/ directory contains complete working examples for BoltzGen workflows: examples/pdl1-boltzgen : PD-L1 protein binder ( protein-anything ) examples/boltzgen-protein : Protein binder design (protocol protein-anything ) examples/boltzgen-cyclic-peptide : Cyclic peptide binder design (protocol peptide-anything ) examples/boltzgen-small-molecule-binder : Small molecule binder design (protocol protein-small_molecule ) examples/boltzgen-nanobody : Nanobody binder design (protocol nanobody-anything ) See the examples/README.md for details.

docs.text: Fold Pulldown An AlphaPulldown-like target × binder pulldown across the shared fold engines (AlphaFold2, Boltz-2, RosettaFold3, Protenix, AlphaFold3, OpenFold3, Chai-1, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-Fast). Previously --method boltz_pulldown This workflow began as Boltz Pulldown, which could only co-fold with Boltz-2. It has since been expanded to run any of the fold engines above, and gained per-chain template matching, multiple samples per pair and a cross-engine score summary. --method boltz_pulldown has been removed; use --method fold_pulldown --methods boltz for the equivalent Boltz-only run. Overview For every target–binder pair the pipeline co-folds the complex with each selected predictor (optionally with multiple seeds / samples per model), then writes: File Contents fold_pulldown/fold_pulldown_scores.tsv One row per predicted structure (canonical fold scores + target , binder ) fold_pulldown/fold_pulldown_summary.tsv One row per (target, binder, tool) with mean/median/max/sd for iptm and ipsae , per-target within-tool z-scores, cross-tool consensus_z , and the z_basis / n_pool / z_pool_small provenance of that z fold_pulldown/fold_pulldown_report.html Simple Quarto overview (boxplots, heatmaps, top hits, cross-tool Spearman) Setup Setup is the same as for Fold . Engine containers and their weights are pulled automatically, except the AlphaFold3 weights ( AlphaFold3 weights ). Local sequence databases are needed only for --msa_method jackhmmer_af2 , or for --msa_method mmseqs2_colabfold without --use_remote_server true . See Fold databases . Example nextflow run Australian-Protein-Design-Initiative/nf-binder-design \ --method fold_pulldown \ --targets targets.fasta \ --binders binders.fasta \ --methods boltz,rf3,protenix \ --create_target_msa true \ --msa_method jackhmmer_af2 \ --n_predictions 5 \ --outdir results \ -profile slurm,m3 Multiple sequence alignments MSA cost is O(N_targets + N_binders) , not O(N × M): each sequence is searched once. Binders are treated as having no useful homologs (query-only MSA unless --create_binder_msa is set). The pipeline never builds a joint paired alignment; each chain is rendered on its own, and an engine pairs rows only in the cases below. FASTA header ids are used as per-chain filenames and are sanitised (non [a-zA-Z0-9_.-] characters become _ ) before use. The pipeline will fail early with a warning is there are duplicate ids within --targets or --binders , or an id is present in both --targets and --binders (after sanitisation). Since output complexes are named with <target>_and_<binder> , ids that contain _and_ may be rejected if they would be ambiguous. Taxonomic pairing Pairing is done by the fold engine, from per-chain files, and only when both chains have homologs that share a taxonomy id. For de novo binder 'pulldowns' where we typically don't use a binder MSA ( --create_binder_msa false ), the taxonomy is not used. The pairing process uses the same heuristics as in Fold : RF3 TaxID= a3m, Protenix species-mnemonic a3m, Boltz key,sequence CSV, and the AF3 / OpenFold3 / Chai-1 equivalents. Condition Pairing --create_binder_msa false (the default) None. Chain B is the binder sequence alone. Boltz is also given msa: empty for chain B, including when --use_msa_server is set, so the server does not fetch a binder MSA either. When the binder sequence equals the target, both chains are given the target MSA: Boltz rejects a homodimer whose copies name different MSAs. --create_target_msa false None for the MSAs this pipeline builds: chain A is a single sequence too. The exception is Boltz with both --use_msa_server and --create_binder_msa true , which fetches and pairs both chains itself. Both --create_target_msa and --create_binder_msa , --msa_method jackhmmer_af2 , and boltz , rf3 , protenix , af3 , openfold3 , chai1 or esmfold2 The engine pairs shared taxids. Jackhmmer headers carry TaxID= / species mnemonics; each chain is still written independently and the engine matches them. Same flags, but af2 or af2_mono None. Those engines always write the binder chain query-only, whatever --create_binder_msa is. If they are the only selected --methods , the binder search is skipped. Both MSAs requested, --msa_method mmseqs2_colabfold None. ColabFold headers carry no taxonomy, so the renders stay unpaired. Boltz with --use_msa_server and --create_binder_msa true still fetches and pairs its own MSAs. esmfold2_fast , or esmfold2 with --esmfold2_single_sequence None. Those runs fold from sequence alone. Template structures When a target's structure is known, pass it with --templates (a directory or glob of .pdb / .cif files, e.g. the target PDBs themselves). Templates are matched to target chains automatically by sequence; see Templates . In a pulldown: Only the target chain is templated by default. --binder_templates true also matches binder chains against the same files, e.g. when a complex structure includes a known binder. Boltz constrains templated chains close to their template by default ( --boltz_template_force , 1.0 Å), because the chain structures are known and the binding pose is what is being predicted. Pass --boltz_template_force false to let Boltz depart from them. Matching cutoffs are the same as in --method fold ( Match cutoffs ): identity and coverage of at least 0.3, at least 40 aligned residues, and the best 4 templates per chain. Every engine except ESMFold2 uses templates, most of them up to 4 per chain ( how each engine uses them ). Command-line options nextflow run Australian-Protein-Design-Initiative/nf-binder-design \ --method fold_pulldown --help Required Flag Description --targets FASTA of target sequences. Optional with --complex_structures (see Supplied complexes ) --binders FASTA of binder sequences, or --complex_structures instead Common options Flag Default Description --methods boltz Comma-separated: af2 , af2_mono , boltz , rf3 , protenix , af3 , openfold3 , chai1 , esmfold2 , esmfold2_fast (see Choosing engines ; ESMFold2 weights and caveats are covered in ESMFold2 ) --af3_model_dir models/alphafold3 AlphaFold3 weights directory ( af3 only; see AlphaFold3 weights ) --af3_paired_msa / --af3_templates / --af3_run_data_pipeline true / inline / false How AF3 is fed and run. -profile af3_germinal_parity sets the combination Germinal uses (pairing off, AF3's own template search, data pipeline on) and needs --af3_db_dir ; see Germinal: external folding validation --msa_method jackhmmer_af2 jackhmmer_af2 or mmseqs2_colabfold --create_target_msa false Build MSA for each target --target_msa none An A3M for the target, built elsewhere, used instead of searching for one. Its first record must be the target sequence. Only one target: a run with several stops, since one file cannot describe them all. Not usable with --create_target_msa --create_binder_msa false Build MSA for each binder (usually leave off for de novo binders). AF2/ af2_mono always fold the binder chain query-only regardless of this flag (see bin/fold/assemble_af2_multimer_msas.py ); if AF2/ af2_mono are the only selected --methods , the pipeline warns and skips building the binder MSA entirely. --n_predictions 5 Samples per complex per method. Matches the native default of the diffusion engines, and with --af2_keep_models all it is what AF2's single run already produces --skip_engens true EnGens is off by default (would emit N × M reports) --consensus_metric ipsae ipsae or iptm ; which metric's per-tool z-scores are averaged into consensus_z --z_stat max max or mean ; the per-complex statistic over samples that gets standardised --z_scope target target standardises within (target, tool) ; global pools all targets into one distribution --min_pool 10 Pools containing fewer complexes than this threshold are flagged z_pool_small in the summary table Every pair is a 2-chain complex, so af2 and af2_mono under --msa_method jackhmmer_af2 both need a uniprot/ -bearing --af2_db_path (default alphafold_20211129 ; the Fold workflow instead defaults to alphafold_20240229 , which is monomer-only). Target MSAs for AF2 are built once (jackhmmer, or a ColabFold/mmseqs2 a3m converted into AF2's per-chain format) and combined with the query-only binder chain into one AF2 multimer input per pair. Every method-specific flag documented under --method fold --help ( --af2_* , --boltz_* , --rf3_* , --protenix_* , --af3_* , --openfold3_* , --chai1_* , --esmfold2_* ) applies here too: the same engines run per target×binder pair instead of per input FASTA. --af2_keep_models controls which of AF2's 5 models per run are kept. It defaults to all here, so one AF2 execution yields the 5 structures specified by --n_predictions without additional runs ( --method fold defaults to best ). For af2_mono , best is typically preferred: without an initial guess, monomer models frequently fail to dock, and ranking isolates docked poses from failed predictions. Output Default layout under --outdir ( params.json and logs/ are written to the outdir root, alongside fold_pulldown/ ): results/ ├── params.json ├── logs/ └── fold_pulldown/ ├── pairs.tsv # id, target, binder (one row per co-folded pair) ├── msa/<msa_method>/ # shared target + binder MSAs ├── msa/paired/ # per-chain MSA rendered into each engine's native format ├── <tool>/<target>_and_<binder>/ # per-tool, per-pair engine outputs (raw + confidence JSON) ├── <tool>/<tool>_fold_scores.tsv # per-tool score table ├── predictions/ # flat gather: <tool>_<target>_and_<binder>_*.cif ├── fold_pulldown_scores.tsv # master score table: one row per predicted structure ├── fold_pulldown_summary.tsv # one row per (target, binder, tool) └── fold_pulldown_report.html # Quarto overview Each co-folded pair receives a complex identifier <target>_and_<binder> (derived from sanitised FASTA headers), used for its <tool>/<target>_and_<binder>/ directory and as the stem for predicted structures in predictions/ . pairs.tsv maps each ID back to its target and binder , facilitating downstream joins against fold_pulldown_scores.tsv . msa/paired/ contains per-chain renders (RF3 TaxID= a3m, Protenix mnemonic-headers a3m, Boltz key,sequence CSV). Each chain is generated independently; pairing behavior is detailed in Taxonomic pairing . AF3, OpenFold3, Chai-1, and ESMFold2 re-render their pairing input within the predict task and do not publish separate MSAs here. Supplied complexes Binders can come from existing target-binder complexes rather than a FASTA. The binder chain of each complex is folded against every target as usual, and the complex is then the reference its predictions are compared against. nextflow run main.nf --method fold_pulldown \ --complex_structures 'complexes/*.pdb' \ --binder_chains B \ --targets targets.fasta \ --methods boltz,rf3 This answers "does this binder still sit the same way against a different target". Each binder yields one comparison per (target, engine, sample), all against the one complex it came from, written to complex_rmsd.tsv : Column Meaning id The binder, named after the complex it came from target Which target this row was folded against. With several targets a binder has one row each, and this is what tells them apart tool , batch , model Which engine, seed job and sample the row describes target_aligned_binder_rmsd_all Superimpose on the target, then score the binder. The pose metric target_aligned_binder_tm_score_all TM-score for the same comparison target_aligned_binder_dockq DockQ for the predicted interface against the reference. The usual reading is <0.23 incorrect, 0.23-0.49 acceptable, 0.49-0.80 medium, >=0.80 high target_aligned_binder_dockq_fnat / _fnonnat / _irmsd / _lrmsd DockQ's components target_aligned_binder_interface_lddt Interface lDDT target_aligned_binder_clash_count Clashes in the predicted complex complex_rmsd_all / complex_tm_score_all Whole-complex comparison. nan when the target folded against differs in length from the complex's own target chain, since those columns need equal lengths; the target-aligned columns above are unaffected Each RMSD and TM-score column also has a _pruned variant, scored over the anchors superimpose_homologs kept rather than all of them. --refold_dockq false drops the DockQ, interface lDDT and clash columns. Flag Default Description --complex_structures Complexes ( .pdb / .cif ; directory or glob). Mutually exclusive with --binders --binder_chains Binder chain id(s), comma-separated. Required. Several chains means several binder records per complex, named <complex>_<chain> --target_chains the non-binder chain Chain used as the superposition reference. A single chain id, or auto Choosing the target chain By default the target is whichever chain is not a binder chain, so a two-chain complex needs only --binder_chains . Give --target_chains explicitly when a complex holds more than two chains, or the run stops rather than guessing which to superimpose on. --target_chains auto resolves the chain per complex by matching each one against the --targets records, which is what mixed-source complexes with inconsistent chain naming need. It is opt-in because a wrong silent pick yields a plausible-looking RMSD against the wrong molecule. The chain it chose is logged for every complex, and a match below 50% identity warns. Targets are optional here Without --targets , the targets are read back out of the complexes' own target chains and deduplicated by sequence, which covers the plain "refold what I gave you" case. If the complexes turn out to hold more than one distinct target the run stops: a pulldown folds every binder against every target, so deriving several would fold mostly meaningless pairs. Pass --targets to say which to use. Two-chain complexes only --target_chains takes one chain. A pulldown folds two-chain pairs (target as chain A, binder as chain B), so a multi-chain target cannot be predicted and there would be nothing to superimpose a second target chain onto. Interpreting scores Different predictors use distinct raw score ranges. The summary table provides within-tool z-scores ( iptm_z , ipsae_z ) so complexes can be evaluated on a common scale within each model, along with consensus_z (the mean per-tool z-score for a given complex) for cross-model ranking. Both z-columns are recorded regardless of which metric defines consensus_z . The two aggregations are separate: --z_stat selects the statistic across samples within a tool ( max by default), and consensus_z averages the resulting z-scores across tools. Ranking behavior is governed by three primary settings: --consensus_metric ipsae : ipSAE ( Dunbrack 2025 ) normalises by interface size and isolates interface quality from whole-complex confidence. Specify --consensus_metric iptm to rank on ipTM instead. --z_stat max : individual diffusion samples per complex exhibit stochastic variation, so standardising the top-scoring sample is typically preferred over the mean. Increasing --n_predictions provides additional sampling depth. Specify --z_stat mean for sample averages, noting that low-scoring outlier conformations can reduce the mean. --z_scope target : pools scores within each target, avoiding distortions from baseline score differences across divergent target proteins. To pool all targets into a single distribution, specify --z_scope global . Each summary row records z_basis (metric, statistic, and scope, e.g. ipsae_max/target ), n_pool (the number of complexes that contributed values to that z-score's --consensus_metric ), and z_pool_small ( True when the pool contains fewer complexes than --min_pool ). With k complexes in a pool, the maximum possible absolute z-score is ( k −1)/√ k ; consequently, a two-complex pool yields only ±0.707 and reflects rank ordering alone. consensus_z falls back from --consensus_metric to the alternate metric only when an entire (target, tool) pool lacks the primary metric (such as a tool that does not emit ipsae ), never on a per-complex basis. This ensures each complex's z-score is calculated consistently with other complexes in its pool. consensus_z_metric records the metric used for each row, and n_tools records the number of tools contributing to consensus_z . iptm_sd and ipsae_sd remain blank for complexes with only one replicate. For downstream statistical modeling or score calibration, use fold_pulldown_scores.tsv and fold_pulldown_summary.tsv directly; the HTML report provides a streamlined summary. docs.text: An AlphaPulldown-like target × binder pulldown across the shared fold engines (AlphaFold2, Boltz-2, RosettaFold3, Protenix, AlphaFold3, OpenFold3, Chai-1, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-Fast). Previously --method boltz_pulldown This workflow began as Boltz Pulldown, which could only co-fold with Boltz-2. It has since been expanded to run any of the fold engines above, and gained per-chain template matching, multiple samples per pair and a cross-engine score summary. --method boltz_pulldown has been removed; use --method fold_pulldown --methods boltz for the equivalent Boltz-only run.

docs.text: For every target–binder pair the pipeline co-folds the complex with each selected predictor (optionally with multiple seeds / samples per model), then writes: File Contents fold_pulldown/fold_pulldown_scores.tsv One row per predicted structure (canonical fold scores + target , binder ) fold_pulldown/fold_pulldown_summary.tsv One row per (target, binder, tool) with mean/median/max/sd for iptm and ipsae , per-target within-tool z-scores, cross-tool consensus_z , and the z_basis / n_pool / z_pool_small provenance of that z fold_pulldown/fold_pulldown_report.html Simple Quarto overview (boxplots, heatmaps, top hits, cross-tool Spearman)

docs.text: nextflow run Australian-Protein-Design-Initiative/nf-binder-design \ --method fold_pulldown \ --targets targets.fasta \ --binders binders.fasta \ --methods boltz,rf3,protenix \ --create_target_msa true \ --msa_method jackhmmer_af2 \ --n_predictions 5 \ --outdir results \ -profile slurm,m3

docs.text: MSA cost is O(N_targets + N_binders) , not O(N × M): each sequence is searched once. Binders are treated as having no useful homologs (query-only MSA unless --create_binder_msa is set). The pipeline never builds a joint paired alignment; each chain is rendered on its own, and an engine pairs rows only in the cases below. FASTA header ids are used as per-chain filenames and are sanitised (non [a-zA-Z0-9_.-] characters become _ ) before use. The pipeline will fail early with a warning is there are duplicate ids within --targets or --binders , or an id is present in both --targets and --binders (after sanitisation). Since output complexes are named with <target>_and_<binder> , ids that contain _and_ may be rejected if they would be ambiguous.
docs.title: Multiple sequence alignments

docs.text: Pairing is done by the fold engine, from per-chain files, and only when both chains have homologs that share a taxonomy id. For de novo binder 'pulldowns' where we typically don't use a binder MSA ( --create_binder_msa false ), the taxonomy is not used. The pairing process uses the same heuristics as in Fold : RF3 TaxID= a3m, Protenix species-mnemonic a3m, Boltz key,sequence CSV, and the AF3 / OpenFold3 / Chai-1 equivalents. Condition Pairing --create_binder_msa false (the default) None. Chain B is the binder sequence alone. Boltz is also given msa: empty for chain B, including when --use_msa_server is set, so the server does not fetch a binder MSA either. When the binder sequence equals the target, both chains are given the target MSA: Boltz rejects a homodimer whose copies name different MSAs. --create_target_msa false None for the MSAs this pipeline builds: chain A is a single sequence too. The exception is Boltz with both --use_msa_server and --create_binder_msa true , which fetches and pairs both chains itself. Both --create_target_msa and --create_binder_msa , --msa_method jackhmmer_af2 , and boltz , rf3 , protenix , af3 , openfold3 , chai1 or esmfold2 The engine pairs shared taxids. Jackhmmer headers carry TaxID= / species mnemonics; each chain is still written independently and the engine matches them. Same flags, but af2 or af2_mono None. Those engines always write the binder chain query-only, whatever --create_binder_msa is. If they are the only selected --methods , the binder search is skipped. Both MSAs requested, --msa_method mmseqs2_colabfold None. ColabFold headers carry no taxonomy, so the renders stay unpaired. Boltz with --use_msa_server and --create_binder_msa true still fetches and pairs its own MSAs. esmfold2_fast , or esmfold2 with --esmfold2_single_sequence None. Those runs fold from sequence alone.
docs.title: Taxonomic pairing

docs.text: When a target's structure is known, pass it with --templates (a directory or glob of .pdb / .cif files, e.g. the target PDBs themselves). Templates are matched to target chains automatically by sequence; see Templates . In a pulldown: Only the target chain is templated by default. --binder_templates true also matches binder chains against the same files, e.g. when a complex structure includes a known binder. Boltz constrains templated chains close to their template by default ( --boltz_template_force , 1.0 Å), because the chain structures are known and the binding pose is what is being predicted. Pass --boltz_template_force false to let Boltz depart from them. Matching cutoffs are the same as in --method fold ( Match cutoffs ): identity and coverage of at least 0.3, at least 40 aligned residues, and the best 4 templates per chain. Every engine except ESMFold2 uses templates, most of them up to 4 per chain ( how each engine uses them ).

docs.text: Flag Description --targets FASTA of target sequences. Optional with --complex_structures (see Supplied complexes ) --binders FASTA of binder sequences, or --complex_structures instead

docs.text: Flag Default Description --methods boltz Comma-separated: af2 , af2_mono , boltz , rf3 , protenix , af3 , openfold3 , chai1 , esmfold2 , esmfold2_fast (see Choosing engines ; ESMFold2 weights and caveats are covered in ESMFold2 ) --af3_model_dir models/alphafold3 AlphaFold3 weights directory ( af3 only; see AlphaFold3 weights ) --af3_paired_msa / --af3_templates / --af3_run_data_pipeline true / inline / false How AF3 is fed and run. -profile af3_germinal_parity sets the combination Germinal uses (pairing off, AF3's own template search, data pipeline on) and needs --af3_db_dir ; see Germinal: external folding validation --msa_method jackhmmer_af2 jackhmmer_af2 or mmseqs2_colabfold --create_target_msa false Build MSA for each target --target_msa none An A3M for the target, built elsewhere, used instead of searching for one. Its first record must be the target sequence. Only one target: a run with several stops, since one file cannot describe them all. Not usable with --create_target_msa --create_binder_msa false Build MSA for each binder (usually leave off for de novo binders). AF2/ af2_mono always fold the binder chain query-only regardless of this flag (see bin/fold/assemble_af2_multimer_msas.py ); if AF2/ af2_mono are the only selected --methods , the pipeline warns and skips building the binder MSA entirely. --n_predictions 5 Samples per complex per method. Matches the native default of the diffusion engines, and with --af2_keep_models all it is what AF2's single run already produces --skip_engens true EnGens is off by default (would emit N × M reports) --consensus_metric ipsae ipsae or iptm ; which metric's per-tool z-scores are averaged into consensus_z --z_stat max max or mean ; the per-complex statistic over samples that gets standardised --z_scope target target standardises within (target, tool) ; global pools all targets into one distribution --min_pool 10 Pools containing fewer complexes than this threshold are flagged z_pool_small in the summary table Every pair is a 2-chain complex, so af2 and af2_mono under --msa_method jackhmmer_af2 both need a uniprot/ -bearing --af2_db_path (default alphafold_20211129 ; the Fold workflow instead defaults to alphafold_20240229 , which is monomer-only). Target MSAs for AF2 are built once (jackhmmer, or a ColabFold/mmseqs2 a3m converted into AF2's per-chain format) and combined with the query-only binder chain into one AF2 multimer input per pair. Every method-specific flag documented under --method fold --help ( --af2_* , --boltz_* , --rf3_* , --protenix_* , --af3_* , --openfold3_* , --chai1_* , --esmfold2_* ) applies here too: the same engines run per target×binder pair instead of per input FASTA. --af2_keep_models controls which of AF2's 5 models per run are kept. It defaults to all here, so one AF2 execution yields the 5 structures specified by --n_predictions without additional runs ( --method fold defaults to best ). For af2_mono , best is typically preferred: without an initial guess, monomer models frequently fail to dock, and ranking isolates docked poses from failed predictions.

docs.text: Default layout under --outdir ( params.json and logs/ are written to the outdir root, alongside fold_pulldown/ ): results/ ├── params.json ├── logs/ └── fold_pulldown/ ├── pairs.tsv # id, target, binder (one row per co-folded pair) ├── msa/<msa_method>/ # shared target + binder MSAs ├── msa/paired/ # per-chain MSA rendered into each engine's native format ├── <tool>/<target>_and_<binder>/ # per-tool, per-pair engine outputs (raw + confidence JSON) ├── <tool>/<tool>_fold_scores.tsv # per-tool score table ├── predictions/ # flat gather: <tool>_<target>_and_<binder>_*.cif ├── fold_pulldown_scores.tsv # master score table: one row per predicted structure ├── fold_pulldown_summary.tsv # one row per (target, binder, tool) └── fold_pulldown_report.html # Quarto overview Each co-folded pair receives a complex identifier <target>_and_<binder> (derived from sanitised FASTA headers), used for its <tool>/<target>_and_<binder>/ directory and as the stem for predicted structures in predictions/ . pairs.tsv maps each ID back to its target and binder , facilitating downstream joins against fold_pulldown_scores.tsv . msa/paired/ contains per-chain renders (RF3 TaxID= a3m, Protenix mnemonic-headers a3m, Boltz key,sequence CSV). Each chain is generated independently; pairing behavior is detailed in Taxonomic pairing . AF3, OpenFold3, Chai-1, and ESMFold2 re-render their pairing input within the predict task and do not publish separate MSAs here.

docs.text: Binders can come from existing target-binder complexes rather than a FASTA. The binder chain of each complex is folded against every target as usual, and the complex is then the reference its predictions are compared against. nextflow run main.nf --method fold_pulldown \ --complex_structures 'complexes/*.pdb' \ --binder_chains B \ --targets targets.fasta \ --methods boltz,rf3 This answers "does this binder still sit the same way against a different target". Each binder yields one comparison per (target, engine, sample), all against the one complex it came from, written to complex_rmsd.tsv : Column Meaning id The binder, named after the complex it came from target Which target this row was folded against. With several targets a binder has one row each, and this is what tells them apart tool , batch , model Which engine, seed job and sample the row describes target_aligned_binder_rmsd_all Superimpose on the target, then score the binder. The pose metric target_aligned_binder_tm_score_all TM-score for the same comparison target_aligned_binder_dockq DockQ for the predicted interface against the reference. The usual reading is <0.23 incorrect, 0.23-0.49 acceptable, 0.49-0.80 medium, >=0.80 high target_aligned_binder_dockq_fnat / _fnonnat / _irmsd / _lrmsd DockQ's components target_aligned_binder_interface_lddt Interface lDDT target_aligned_binder_clash_count Clashes in the predicted complex complex_rmsd_all / complex_tm_score_all Whole-complex comparison. nan when the target folded against differs in length from the complex's own target chain, since those columns need equal lengths; the target-aligned columns above are unaffected Each RMSD and TM-score column also has a _pruned variant, scored over the anchors superimpose_homologs kept rather than all of them. --refold_dockq false drops the DockQ, interface lDDT and clash columns.
